ex.s: Not long ago, my fifth-grade son Kevin asked me about the meaning of a word in a novel.

ex.s: I looked pointedly at the bookshelf that held at least three dictionaries, and Kevin sighed dramatically.
ex.t: 我特意看了看那个至少放着三本词典的书架，凯文夸张地叹了口气。

ex.s: I took down one of the dictionaries, and we read it together for a few minutes before I handed it to him.
ex.t: 我取下一本词典，和他一起读了几分钟，然后把它交给了他。

ex.s: It took him a few tries to find the word in question.
ex.t: 他试了好几次才找到要查的那个词。

ex.s: While going through the pages, he kept saying, wide-eyed: “How can there be this many words?” After a while, he looked at me and asked, “Do you know all these words, Mom?” I smiled, “I definitely do not know all these words,” I said.
ex.t: 翻页的时候，他睁大眼睛不停地说：“怎么会有这么多词？”过了一会儿，他看着我问：“妈妈，这些词你都认识吗？”我笑了笑说：“我当然不可能全都认识。”

ex.s: Kevin wanted to see the dictionary.
ex.t: 凯文想看看那本词典。

ex.s: I felt a small pain in my chest The dictionary was stolen at the end of my freshman year of college.
ex.t: 我胸口隐隐作痛——那本词典在我大一结束时被偷了。

ex.s: “That’s so sad,” he said, “but you still know all those words, even without the book.” I realized that this was true.
ex.t: “那太遗憾了，”他说，“不过即使没有那本书，你依然认识那些词。”我意识到这话确实没错。

ex.s: I still made it through the next three years of college, even without the book.
ex.t: 即使没有那本书，我也顺利读完了大学剩下的三年。

ex.s: And it wasn't, ultimately, the dictionary that got me there — not really.
ex.t: 说到底，真正让我走到今天的并不是那本词典——并不是。

ex.s: It’s not about the words themselves or how we learn them, but the wanting to know them, the curiosity and the appetite.
ex.t: 重要的不是单词本身，也不是我们如何学习它们，而是那份想了解它们的渴望、好奇心和求知欲。

ex.s: Oaks and sweetgums, which currently account for a majority of the city’s trees, produce huge amounts of a chemical substance called isoprene.

ex.s: The research, carried out by scientists at the Columbia Climate School and other institutions, found that if the city maintains past species patterns in new plantings, isoprene production in Manhattan in coming decades will go up by about 140%, and resulting summer ozone levels as much as 30%.

ex.s: In the study, 187 people were invited to visit Kettle’s Yard gallery during an exhibition of handmade clay objects.
ex.t: 在这项研究中，187人受邀在手工陶艺品展览期间参观了Kettle's Yard美术馆。

ex.s: Participants were randomly divided into two groups: the “beauty” group was asked to actively consider and then rate the beauty of each object they viewed, while the control group just matched a line drawing of the object with the artwork itself.
ex.t: 参与者被随机分成两组：“美感”组被要求主动思考并评价每件所见物品的美，而对照组只是把物品的线描图与艺术品本身进行匹配。

ex.s: Across all participants, those in the beauty group scored almost 14% higher on average than the control group in abstract thinking.
ex.t: 在所有参与者中，美感组在抽象思维上的平均得分比对照组高出近14%。

ex.s: While they were told the study was about cognitive processes, participants were asked about interests, with around half saying they had an artistic hobby.
ex.t: 虽然参与者被告知该研究是关于认知过程的，但他们也被问及兴趣爱好，约一半人说自己有艺术爱好。

ex.s: Among those, the effect was greater: those with an artistic hobby in the beauty group scored over 25% higher on average for abstract thinking than those with an artistic hobby in the control group.
ex.t: 在这些人中，效果更明显：美感组中有艺术爱好的人，其抽象思维平均得分比对照组中有艺术爱好的人高出25%以上。

ex.s: Emotional states of participants were also measured by asking about their feelings while completing the gallery task.
ex.t: 研究人员还通过询问参与者完成美术馆任务时的感受，测量了他们的情绪状态。

ex.s: Across all participants, those in the beauty group reported an average of 23% higher levels of “transformative and self-transcendent feelings” — such as feeling moved, enlightened and inspired — than the control group.
ex.t: 在所有参与者中，美感组报告的“蜕变性和超越自我的感受”——如感动、受启迪、受鼓舞——平均比对照组高出23%。

ex.s: Importantly, however, the beauty group did not report feeling any happier than the control group, suggesting that it was the engagement with beauty that influenced abstract thinking, rather than any overall positivity from the experience.
ex.t: 然而重要的是，美感组并没有报告比对照组更快乐，这表明影响抽象思维的是与美的接触，而不是这次经历带来的整体积极情绪。

ex.s: “We usually think in very concrete terms when doing something on a screen,” said Simone Schnall, senior author of the study.
ex.t: “我们在屏幕上做事时，通常以非常具体的方式思考，”该研究的资深作者Simone Schnall说。

ex.s: “It’s becoming much rarer to zone out and just let the mind wander, but that’s when we think in ways that broaden our minds.
ex.t: “放空自己、任思绪自由漫游的机会越来越少，但那正是我们以开阔思维的方式思考的时候。

ex.s: Admiring the beauty of art may be the ideal way to initiate the abstract cognitive processes.”
ex.t: 欣赏艺术之美或许是启动抽象认知过程的理想方式。”

ex.s: The blinding whiteout made driving nearly impossible.
ex.t: 令人眩目的白茫一片让驾驶几乎无法进行。

ex.s: After a struggle, she managed to free the vehicle and continued inching along the snow-covered road.
ex.t: 经过一番努力，她设法把车弄了出来，继续在积雪覆盖的道路上缓慢前行。

ex.s: Seeing no hope of immediate rescue, Emily decided to spend the night in her car.
ex.t: 眼看没有立即获救的希望，Emily决定在车里过夜。

ex.s: When Emily rolled down the window, Rachel asked if she was okay and told her it was not safe to stay overnight in the car.
ex.t: 当Emily摇下车窗时，Rachel问她是否还好，并告诉她整夜待在车里不安全。

ex.s: Grateful and relieved, Emily accepted the offer.
ex.t: Emily既感激又松了一口气，接受了他们的提议。

ex.s: In the cafe, the couple bought Emily a hot chocolate and listened patiently as she explained her desperate situation: she was about a hundred miles from her destination, her car was completely stuck, and her entire holiday plan could be ruined.
ex.t: 在咖啡馆里，这对夫妇给Emily买了一杯热巧克力，耐心地听她讲述自己的绝境：她离目的地大约还有一百英里，车完全陷住了，整个假期计划可能都要泡汤。

ex.s: The Best Chinese Restaurants Around D.C.
ex.t: 华盛顿特区周边最好的中餐馆

ex.s: The D.C. area is home to many outstanding Chinese restaurants, but diners willing to travel outside the city limits will also be rewarded.
ex.t: 华盛顿特区有许多出色的中餐馆，但愿意走出市区就餐的食客也会有所收获。

ex.s: This not-so-hidden-anymore fine restaurant for Sichuan cuisine is inside the Days Inn off New York Avenue.
ex.t: 这家已不再那么隐秘的川菜精品餐厅位于纽约大道旁的戴斯酒店内。

ex.s: Shanghai Taste offers arguably the best soup dumplings in the area.
ex.t: Shanghai Taste可以说拥有本地区最好吃的汤包。

ex.s: The restaurant is open from 11:00 am to 9:00 pm Tuesday through Sunday, offering call-in orders and pickups.
ex.t: 餐厅周二至周日上午11:00至晚上9:00营业，接受电话订餐和自取。

ex.s: The spacious dining room is regularly filled with customers enjoying dumplings and a variety of noodle and rice dishes.
ex.t: 宽敞的餐厅里常常坐满了享用饺子以及各种面条、米饭菜肴的顾客。

ex.s: What do we know about the Cantonese restaurant in Columbia Heights?
ex.t: 关于哥伦比亚高地的那家粤餐厅，我们知道什么？

ex.s: But that’s not the thing he prides himself on.
ex.t: 但这并不是他引以为傲的事。

ex.s: “I am the last original client of Frank Lloyd Wright, still living in the home he designed for me,” Reisley said, sitting in the bright open living room of the home designed by the famous architect.
ex.t: “我是弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特最后一位健在的原始客户，至今仍住在他为我设计的房子里，”Reisley坐在由这位著名建筑师设计的明亮通透的客厅里说道。

ex.s: The house where Reisley has lived for 73 years is located in the woods of Westchester County, New York, just 30 miles north of Manhattan.
ex.t: Reisley住了73年的房子位于纽约州韦斯特切斯特县的树林里，距曼哈顿以北仅30英里。

ex.s: It’s one of 47 that make up the peaceful mid-20th-century modern village of Usonia.
ex.t: 它是组成Usonia这座宁静的20世纪中期现代风格村庄的47座住宅之一。

ex.s: On their first trip out, they were greeted with such enthusiasm from the 10 families who’d already established homes there that they decided to join.
ex.t: 第一次实地探访时，已在那里安家的10户人家热情相迎，这让他们决定加入。

ex.s: The house has signature Wright features.
ex.t: 这座房子具有赖特的标志性特色。

ex.s: Over the decades, Reisley has opened his doors to visitors.
ex.t: 几十年来，Reisley一直敞开家门欢迎访客。

ex.s: The house is now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
ex.t: 这座房子如今已被列入《国家史迹名录》。

ex.s: He co-founded the Frank Lloyd Wright Building Conservancy, an organization engaged in the preservation of all of Wright’s remaining buildings.
ex.t: 他联合创立了弗兰克·劳埃德·赖特建筑保护协会，该组织致力于保护赖特现存的所有建筑。

ex.s: Reisley believes that his devotion to the home and the community are what have kept him in such good health all of these years.
ex.t: Reisley相信，正是对这座房子和这片社区的热爱，让他多年来一直保持着如此好的健康状态。

ex.s: The convenience of its location.
ex.t: 那里位置的便利。

ex.s: The warmth of its residents.
ex.t: 那里居民的热情。

ex.s: What can be inferred about Reisley from the last paragraph?
ex.t: 从最后一段可以推断出关于Reisley的什么？

ex.s: The peak of Mount Qomolangma, 8,849 meters above sea level.
ex.t: 珠穆朗玛峰峰顶，海拔8849米。

ex.s: Chimborazo, 6,263 m; Mont Blanc, 4,806 m; Pradidali hut, at the foot of the Pala group in the Dolomites, 2,278 m.
ex.t: 钦博拉索山，6263米；勃朗峰，4806米；Pradidali小屋，位于多洛米蒂山脉Pala山群脚下，海拔2278米。

ex.s: But elevation is necessarily relative: only the choice of a reference point allows us to express numerically the height of an object or a location.
ex.t: 但海拔必然是相对的：只有选定一个参照点，我们才能用数字表示一个物体或地点的高度。

ex.s: The idea of sea level as a reference point for elevations has by now been around for so long as to go essentially unnoticed-we mention it without even considering what it means.
ex.t: 以海平面作为海拔参照点的想法由来已久，以至于人们基本不再留意——我们提到它时甚至不会去想它意味着什么。

ex.s: That the concept has a history is easily ignored.
ex.t: 这个概念也有其历史，这一点很容易被忽视。

ex.s: Appropriately, the book took shape during a summer spent between sea and mountains.
ex.t: 巧的是，这本书是在一个往来于大海与群山之间的夏天逐渐成形的。

ex.s: A month after visiting the French Riviera and enjoying the sandy beaches of Nice and Menton, I went hiking with friends in the Pala group.
ex.t: 在游览法国里维埃拉、享受尼斯和芒通的沙滩一个月后，我和朋友们去了Pala山群徒步。

ex.s: Why did they vary ever so slightly from one instrument to the next?
ex.t: 为什么不同仪器上的读数会有细微差别？

ex.s: This sense of uncertainty led me to think about the meaning of zero.
ex.t: 这种不确定感让我开始思考“零”的意义。

ex.s: This is how I began my search for the conceptual history of sea level.
ex.t: 我就是这样开始探寻海平面的概念史的。

ex.s: In this book I examine three crucial stages in the history of mean sea level.
ex.t: 在本书中，我考察了平均海平面历史上的三个关键阶段。

ex.s: These stages mirror the development of human conceptions of the sea.
ex.t: 这些阶段反映了人类对海洋认知的发展。

ex.s: Since I began thinking about this project in August 2011, the issue of sea-level rise and the need to place it historically have only become more urgent: between then and the end of 2022 the global sea rose by almost 5 centimeters, about half of the overall rise recorded by satellites since 1993.
ex.t: 自从2011年8月我开始思考这个项目以来，海平面上升问题以及将其置于历史背景中考察的必要性变得愈发紧迫：从那时到2022年底，全球海平面上升了近5厘米，约为卫星自1993年以来记录的总升幅的一半。

ex.s: What does the author point out at the beginning of the text?
ex.t: 作者在文章开头指出了什么？

ex.s: The concept of elevation is relative.
ex.t: 海拔的概念是相对的。

ex.s: The reference point is hard to locate.
ex.t: 参照点难以确定。

ex.s: How the altimeter was invented.
ex.t: 高度计是如何发明的。

ex.s: What initiated the author’s research.
ex.t: 是什么促使作者开展这项研究。

ex.s: Why the digital readings varied.
ex.t: 数字读数为什么会有差异。

ex.s: Where the author spent his holiday.
ex.t: 作者在哪里度过了假期。

ex.s: What does the underlined word “it” refer to in the last paragraph?
ex.t: 最后一段中划线词“it”指什么？

ex.t: 文中提到的那本书可以取什么书名？

ex.s: The Barcelona subway pulls into the station, the doors slide open and passengers pour out to go about their daily business.
ex.t: 巴塞罗那地铁驶入车站，车门滑开，乘客们鱼贯而出，各自忙碌日常事务。

ex.s: Barcelona has put together a package of clean energy technologies to help public transportation go greener, while also doing its part to tackle climate change and aid Europe’s difficult shift to the privately owned electric vehicle market.
ex.t: 巴塞罗那整合了一整套清洁能源技术，帮助公共交通变得更加环保，同时也为应对气候变化尽一份力，并助力欧洲向私人电动汽车市场的艰难转型。

ex.s: Bernardo Espinoza, an engineer who takes the subway every day, owns an electric car.
ex.t: 每天乘地铁的工程师Bernardo Espinoza拥有一辆电动汽车。

ex.s: “I am pleasantly surprised, because I am always looking for where to plug it in,” Espinoza said before catching the subway in a working-class area of southern Barcelona.
ex.t: “我感到惊喜，因为我总是在找哪里能给它充电，”Espinoza在巴塞罗那南部一个工薪阶层社区乘地铁前说。

ex.s: “And if it is from energy from the trains’ brakes, then even better.”
ex.t: “如果用的是列车刹车产生的能量，那就更好了。”

ex.s: They consist of an electric motor which collects energy used in the braking action that would be lost as heat by conventional brakes.
ex.t: 它由一个电动机组成，可以收集制动过程中产生的能量——这些能量若用传统制动器则会以热量形式散失。

ex.s: Alvaro Luna, a professor of electrical engineering, said that the system is innovative in so far as it allows for recycled energy to be redirected to specific local uses — in this case powering electric cars parked nearby.
ex.t: 电气工程教授Alvaro Luna表示，该系统的创新之处在于，它能把回收的能量重新导向特定的本地用途——在这个案例中就是为停放在附近的电动汽车供电。

ex.s: Why does Barcelona launch the MetroCharge project?
ex.t: 巴塞罗那为什么启动MetroCharge项目？

ex.s: To fuel the city’s economy.
ex.t: 为了推动城市经济发展。

ex.s: To raise the quality of electric cars.
ex.t: 为了提高电动汽车的质量。

ex.s: What did Luna say about the system?
ex.t: Luna对这个系统说了什么？

ex.s: It prioritizes the safety of trains.
ex.t: 它把列车安全放在首位。

ex.s: It generates jobs for the locals.
ex.t: 它为当地人创造了就业机会。

ex.s: If only the effort they put into avoiding responsibility could be redirected into, well, actual responsibility.
ex.t: 要是他们用来逃避责任的那份力气能转移到——嗯——真正的责任上就好了。

ex.s: ● Make housework part of the family routine.
ex.t: ● 让家务成为家庭日常的一部分。

ex.s: Involve your child in the daily running of the house: tidying toys, feeding the dog, watering the plants. ____36____ When the tasks become as routine as brushing teeth, kids internalise that helping with housework is simply part of life.
ex.t: 让孩子参与家庭的日常运转：收拾玩具、喂狗、给植物浇水。____ 当这些任务变得像刷牙一样习以为常，孩子就会内化这样一种观念：帮忙做家务本来就是生活的一部分。

ex.s: You can’t expect your child to tackle their tasks with enthusiasm while you’re complaining about loading the dishwasher.
ex.t: 你不能一边抱怨着把碗碟放进洗碗机，一边指望孩子满怀热情地完成自己的任务。

ex.s: If your child sees you enjoying your work and taking pride in a job well done, they’re far more likely to do the same.
ex.t: 如果孩子看到你在工作中自得其乐、为把事情做好而自豪，他们就更有可能效仿。

ex.s: Few things strike fear into a child’s heart like the prospect of failing.
ex.t: 没什么比害怕失败更让孩子心生恐惧了。

ex.s: The best way is to normalise mistakes as a natural part of learning.
ex.t: 最好的办法是把犯错正常化，视其为学习的自然组成部分。

ex.s: The key is consistency.
ex.t: 关键在于持之以恒。

ex.s: Model the work ethic you want to see.
ex.t: 为孩子示范你希望看到的敬业精神。

ex.s: Sometimes, a cleaner living room is the best reward.
ex.t: 有时候，一个整洁的客厅就是最好的奖励。

ex.s: Not every child is born with the willpower of a marathon runner.
ex.t: 不是每个孩子天生都有马拉松运动员那样的意志力。

ex.s: I didn’t come from a family connected to the ____41____ world, which I perceived as a major ____42____.
ex.t: 我家与____界没有任何联系，我认为这是一个重大的____。

ex.s: And then, at the end of the lesson, one child asked me a question: “Have you always wanted to be a ____46____, Miss?” I explained that when I was his age, I actually wanted to be a writer, but I didn’t think I quite had what it ____47____.
ex.t: 下课时，一个孩子问了我一个问题：“老师，您一直想当____吗？”我解释说，我在他那个年纪时其实想当作家，但我觉得自己不具备那所需要的____。

ex.s: The boy replied with a ____48____ look, “Well, you are telling us to live our dreams when you haven’t even done it yourself.
ex.t: 男孩一脸____地回答：“可您一边告诉我们要为梦想而活，一边自己都没做到。

ex.s: On the basis of that ____53____, I applied to go back to university and study creative writing.
ex.t: 正是基于那次____，我申请重返大学学习创意写作。

ex.s: There were times when I found myself wondering if I should pack it all in, but the boy’s words kept ringing in my ears: I knew I needed nothing else to succeed but a bit of ____54____ and hard work.
ex.t: 有几次我想过要不要干脆放弃，但男孩的话一直在我耳边回响：我知道，成功所需要的不过是一点____和勤奋。

ex.s: In tai chi, the dan tian is your qi core and qi in Chinese means life force.
ex.t: 在太极拳中，丹田是你的气之核心，而“气”在中文里意为生命力。

ex.s: Now, I ____60____ (suppose) to feel the weight on my legs and sink my dan tian.
ex.t: 现在，我____（应该）感受双腿承受的重量，让丹田下沉。

ex.s: We move on to tai chi positions, of ____61____ there are forty-two in the style that Angela teaches.
ex.t: 接着我们练习太极招式，Angela所教的这一流派共有____四十二式。

ex.s: Today, we will only be doing the first nine.
ex.t: 今天我们只练前九式。

ex.s: The movements have ____62____ (describe) names like “holding the bowl” and “grabbing the bird’s tail.”
ex.t: 这些招式有着____（描述性的）名字，比如“抱碗”和“揽雀尾”。

ex.s: Then, Angela gets us to try the nine movements on our own.
ex.t: 然后，Angela让我们自己试着做这九个动作。

ex.s: At the end of the lesson, I feel wide awake, despite it still ____64____ (be) early at 8 am.
ex.t: 课程结束时，尽管才早上8点、仍然____（是）很早，我却感觉神清气爽。

ex.s: I found comfort in keeping myself awake when everyone else had gone to bed, and I loved the silence of the night.
ex.t: 当其他人都睡了，我却在清醒中感到慰藉，我喜爱夜晚的宁静。

ex.s: I still loved the night and would stay up until unruly hours for no apparent reason, chatting online and watching videos.
ex.t: 我依然热爱夜晚，会无缘无故熬到离谱的时间，上网聊天、看视频。

ex.s: When I finally started to study, I would race through the assigned work, often well past midnight.
ex.t: 等我终于开始学习时，我会匆匆忙忙赶完布置的作业，常常早已过了午夜。

ex.s: My roommates would tell me to go to bed and get up early the following morning to do it instead.
ex.t: 室友们会劝我去睡觉，第二天早上早点起来再做。

ex.s: Bent over my laptop while sitting on the bed in the corner of my room, I suddenly felt a pounding headache, and had to lie down.
ex.t: 我弓着背坐在房间角落的床上盯着笔记本电脑，突然感到一阵剧烈的头痛，不得不躺下。

ex.s: Unable to keep my eyes open, I decided I had no choice but to finish my homework the next morning.
ex.t: 眼睛都睁不开了，我决定别无选择，只能第二天早上再完成作业。

ex.s: At the school clinic, a doctor, with a serious expression on his face, handed me a medical report.
ex.t: 在校医务室，一位医生表情严肃地递给我一份体检报告。

ex.s: Struck by the doctor’s warning, I knew I had to make a change.
ex.t: 医生的警告让我警醒，我知道自己必须做出改变。

ex.s: Slowly but surely, my efforts to adjust to the new routine paid off.
ex.t: 我努力适应新作息，缓慢但稳步地见到了成效。

ex.s: The City of Burlington public art program is presenting a series of temporary public art signs at the Beachway in conjunction with the Ontario Culture Days.
ex.t: 伯灵顿市公共艺术项目正与安大略文化日合作，在Beachway推出一系列临时公共艺术标牌。

ex.t: 该项目将选出10名视觉艺术家和10名作家，创作将在多功能步道沿线的临时标牌上展出的作品。

ex.s: The artist fee for this project is $400.
ex.t: 本项目的艺术家酬金为400美元。

ex.s: Often students come to the classroom believing that learning can’t be fun and that what they learn isn’t relevant to the real world — much less to their personal interests.
ex.t: 学生们常常带着这样的看法走进教室：学习不可能有趣，所学内容与现实世界无关——更谈不上与他们的个人兴趣有关。

ex.s: No matter what subject I’m teaching, I find ways to bring my hobbies into the classroom.
ex.t: 无论教什么科目，我都会想办法把我的爱好带进课堂。

ex.s: But I quickly learned that the practice also helped me build stronger relationships with them.
ex.t: 但我很快发现，这种做法还帮助我与学生建立了更牢固的关系。

ex.s: I find that doing so energizes my instruction, engages my students, and demonstrates to them how abstract concepts play out in the real world.
ex.t: 我发现，这样做让我的教学更有活力，让学生更投入，也向他们展示了抽象概念在现实世界中的实际运用。

ex.t: 作者认为，什么给教师带来了挑战？

ex.t: 课本与学生生活脱节。

ex.t: 老师与学生爱好之间的差距。

ex.t: 作者为什么把轮胎带进课堂？

ex.s: To explain the structure of a car.

ex.s: Human beings have always loved reviews: word of mouth has long been regarded as one of the most valuable marketing tools available to a company.
ex.t: 人类向来喜欢评价：口碑长期以来一直被视为公司最有价值的营销工具之一。

ex.s: The study used a dataset of 1,600 reviews of Chicago hotels.
ex.t: 该研究使用了一个包含1600条芝加哥酒店评论的数据集。

ex.s: The reviews were presented to 400 subjects.
ex.t: 这些评论被呈现给400名受试者。

ex.s: The reviews were written by real people who were given information about the hotel.
ex.t: 这些评论由真人撰写，他们事先获得了有关酒店的信息。

ex.s: The results show that consumers generally trust negative reviews more than positive ones.

ex.t: 该研究的主要作者、斯坦福人文与科学学院生物学助理教授巴纳巴斯·达鲁说：“随着科技的发展，人们很容易借助手机应用观察不同的物种。”

ex.s: Their study revealed that the large number of observation-only records did not lead to better global coverage.
ex.t: 他们的研究表明，大量仅基于观察的记录并没有带来更好的全球覆盖。

ex.s: This makes sense because the people who get observational biodiversity data on mobile devices are often citizen scientists recording their encounters with species in areas nearby.
ex.t: 这是有道理的，因为通过移动设备获取生物多样性观察数据的人，往往是记录自己在附近地区偶遇物种的公民科学家。

ex.s: What can we do with the imperfect datasets of biodiversity?
ex.t: 面对这些不完美的生物多样性数据集，我们能做些什么？

ex.s: To improve the quality of observational data, biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image.”
ex.t: 为了提高观察数据的质量，生物多样性应用还可以鼓励用户请专家确认其上传图片的物种鉴定。”

ex.s: What do we know about the records of species collected now?
ex.t: 关于目前收集的物种记录，我们了解到什么？

ex.s: What has led to the biases according to the study?
ex.t: 根据这项研究，是什么导致了偏差？

ex.s: Hire experts to check the records.

ex.t: 看着排队上车的人越来越少，一种无助感涌上我的心头。

ex.t: 这时，冈特指了指汽车站的候车大厅。

ex.s: There, at the entrance, was a cash machine.
ex.t: 就在入口处，有一台自动取款机。

ex.s: I jumped out of the car, made a mad run for the machine, and popped my card in, only to read the message: "Out of order.
ex.t: 我跳下车，拼命跑向取款机，把卡插了进去，结果只看到一条信息：“故障。

ex.s: I ran back to Gunter and told him the bad news.

ex.s: “We wanted to do something where we do a call to artists in the Bay Area to submit stories for a contest,” Trost says.
ex.t: 特罗斯特说：“我们想办一个活动，向湾区的艺术家征集故事参加比赛。”

ex.t: 获奖故事将进入我们的自助亭，然后你就成了一名发表过作品的艺术家。”

ex.s: “At the end of the day all transit agencies right now are doing everything they can to improve the rider experience.
ex.t: “归根结底，现在所有公交机构都在竭尽所能改善乘客体验。

ex.s: Why did BART start the kiosk program?
ex.t: BART为什么启动自助亭项目？

ex.t: 自助亭里的故事是如何分类的？

ex.s: However, most produce at the store went through weeks of travel and covered hundreds of miles before reaching the table.
ex.t: 然而，商店里的大多数农产品在端上餐桌之前都经过了数周的运输、跨越了数百英里。

ex.s: While farmer’s markets are a solid choice to reduce the journey, Babylon Micro-Farm (BMF) shortens it even more.
ex.t: 虽然农贸市场是缩短这一路程的可靠选择，但Babylon微型农场（BMF）把这段路程缩得更短。

ex.s: The innovative design requires little effort to achieve a reliable weekly supply of fresh greens.
ex.t: 这一创新设计只需很少的精力就能实现每周稳定供应新鲜蔬菜。

ex.s: By connecting through the Cloud, BMF is remotely monitored.
ex.t: 通过云端连接，BMF可以被远程监控。

ex.s: Because the system is automated, it significantly reduces the amount of water needed to grow plants.
ex.t: 由于系统是自动化的，它大大减少了种植植物所需的水量。

ex.s: Rather than watering rows of soil, the system provides just the right amount to each plant.
ex.t: 系统不是浇灌一排排土壤，而是为每株植物提供恰到好处的水量。

ex.s: In addition, there’s no need for pesticides and other chemicals that pollute traditional farms and the surrounding environment.
ex.t: 此外，还不需要杀虫剂和其他污染传统农场及周边环境的化学品。

ex.s: Inside the office, they encourage recycling and waste reduction by limiting garbage cans and avoiding single-use plastic.
ex.t: 在办公室里，他们通过减少垃圾桶、避免使用一次性塑料来鼓励回收利用和减少浪费。

ex.s: It guarantees the variety of food.
ex.t: 它保证食物的多样性。

ex.s: It cuts the farm-to-table distance.
ex.t: 它缩短了从农场到餐桌的距离。

ex.s: What information does the convenient app offer?
ex.t: 这款便捷的应用提供什么信息？

ex.t: 土壤中的化学污染物。

ex.s: What does the text mainly talk about?
ex.t: 本文主要讲了什么？

ex.s: Given the astonishing potential of AI to transform our lives, we all need to take action to deal with our AI-powered future, and this is where AI by Design: A Plan for Living with Artificial Intelligence comes in.
ex.t: 鉴于人工智能改变我们生活的惊人潜力，我们都需要行动起来应对人工智能驱动的未来，这正是《设计人工智能：与人工智能共处的规划》一书的意义所在。

ex.s: She writes from the practical angle of a business person rather than as an academic, making for a guide which is highly accessible and informative and which, by the close, will make you feel almost as smart as AI.
ex.t: 她以商人的务实角度而非学者的角度写作，使这本指南通俗易懂、内容丰富，读完后会让你觉得自己几乎和人工智能一样聪明。

ex.s: As we soon come to learn from AI by Design AI is already super-smart and will become more capable, moving from the current generation of “narrow-AI” to Artificial General Intelligence.
ex.t: 正如我们很快就能从《设计人工智能》中了解到的那样，人工智能已经超级聪明，并且将变得更强大，从当前的“狭义人工智能”发展到通用人工智能。

ex.s: Campbell’s point is to wake up those responsible for AI—the technology companies and world leaders—so they are on the same page as all the experts currently developing it.
ex.t: 坎贝尔的目的是唤醒那些对人工智能负责的人——科技公司和世界领导人——让他们与目前开发人工智能的所有专家达成共识。

ex.s: AI will affect us all, and if you only read one book on the subject, this is it.
ex.t: 人工智能将影响我们所有人，如果你只读一本关于这个主题的书，那就是这本。

ex.t: 第二段中“In the wrong hands”这个短语可能是什么意思？

ex.t: 阐明人工智能的定义。

ex.s: Travel promotes understanding, expands our minds, makes us better people, and boosts local economies and communities, but the rapid growth of travel has led to overtourism in certain regions and destinations. ___16___ Certainly not.

ex.s: The loss of what travel offers would be unacceptable in today’s world.
ex.t: 在当今世界，失去旅行带来的一切是不可接受的。

ex.s: Here are some tips on making wise decisions to minimize pressure on the places we visit and improve our experience.
ex.t: 以下是一些建议，帮助你做出明智的决定，减轻我们游览之地的压力，并提升我们的体验。

ex.s: With so many online posts featuring the same places, it’s easy to feel like you’re missing out.
ex.t: 网上有那么多展示同一批地方的帖子，你很容易觉得自己错过了什么。

ex.t: 只有当风景、文化或美食深深吸引你时，才去那个地方。____

ex.s: The best way to ease pressure on over-touristed destinations is to go somewhere else.
ex.t: 缓解游客过多目的地压力的最好办法，是去别的地方。

ex.s: Though overtourism is described as a problem affecting the entire world, it’s actually concentrated to a small number of extremely popular spots.
ex.t: 尽管过度旅游被描述为一个影响全世界的问题，但它实际上集中在极少数极受欢迎的景点。

ex.s: You’ll compete with fewer tourists, save money, experience a different side of a popular place, and boost the economy when tourism is traditionally slower.
ex.t: 你将与更少的游客竞争，还能省钱，体验热门地方不一样的一面，并在传统旅游淡季提振当地经济。

ex.s: Do your part to preserve what makes a destination special in the first place. ___20___ You may be amazed how much closer you’ll feel to the people there.

ex.s: The government has struggled to come up with measures to address the problem, particularly in the poorer, rural areas east of the Volga River, including arranging doctor’s appointments by video chat and expanding financial aid programs to motivate doctors to practice medicine in remote parts of the country like Krasnoyarsk.

ex.s: The annual arrival of the Saint Lukas is another attempt to improve the situation.
ex.t: 圣卢卡斯每年的到来是改善这一状况的又一次尝试。

ex.s: “I didn’t like the ending,” I said to my favorite college professor.
ex.t: "我不喜欢这个结局，"我对我最喜欢的大学教授说。

ex.s: I had just finished reading The Mill on the Floss by George Eliot, and I was heartbroken with the ending.
ex.t: 我刚读完乔治·艾略特的《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》，对结局感到心碎。

ex.s: He suggested I think about the difference between endings that I wanted for the characters and endings that were right for the characters, endings that satisfied the story even if they didn’t have a traditionally positive outcome.
ex.t: 他建议我想一想"我希望角色得到的结局"和"适合角色的结局"之间的区别——那些即使没有传统意义上的圆满结局、却能让故事得到满足的结局。

ex.s: Of course, I would have preferred a different ending for Tom and Maggie Tulliver, but the ending they got did make the most sense for them.
ex.t: 当然，我本来希望汤姆和玛吉·塔利弗有一个不同的结局，但他们得到的结局对他们来说确实最合理。

ex.s: This was an aha moment for me, and I never thought about endings the same way again.
ex.t: 这对我来说是一个恍然大悟的时刻，从那以后我再也不会用同样的方式看待结局了。

ex.s: But writing the end — that’s hard.
ex.t: 但是写结局——那很难。

ex.s: You have to balance creating an ending that's unpredictable, but doesn’t seem to come from nowhere, one that fits what’s right for the characters.
ex.t: 你必须平衡：创造一个不可预测但又不能凭空而来的结局，一个适合角色发展的结局。

ex.s: That’s why this issue (期) of Writer’s Digest aims to help you figure out how to write the best ending for whatever kind of writing you’re doing.
ex.t: 所以本期《作家文摘》旨在帮助你弄清楚如何为你正在写的任何类型的作品写出最好的结局。

ex.s: If it’s short stories, Peter Mountford breaks down six techniques you can try to see which one helps you stick the landing.
ex.t: 如果是短篇小说，彼得·蒙特福德拆解了六种技巧，你可以试试看哪种能帮你完美收官。

ex.s: Elizabeth Sims analyzes the final chapters of five great novels to see what key points they include and how you can adapt them for your work.
ex.t: 伊丽莎白·西姆斯分析了五部伟大小说的最后章节，看看它们包含哪些要点，以及你如何将其改编运用到自己的作品中。

ex.s: This issue won’t tell you what your ending should be — that’s up to you and the story you’re telling — but it might provide what you need to get there.
ex.t: 本期不会告诉你你的结局应该是什么——这取决于你和你要讲的故事——但它可能提供你所需要的帮助来实现它。

ex.s: The goal of this book is to make the case for digital minimalism, including a detailed exploration of what it asks and why it works, and then to teach you how to adopt this philosophy if you decide it’s right for you.
ex.t: 本书旨在阐明数字极简主义的主张，包括详细探讨它的要求以及它为何有效，然后教你在认为它适合你的情况下如何践行这一理念。

ex.s: To do so, I divided the book into two parts.
ex.t: 为此，我把这本书分成了两部分。

ex.s: In part one, I describe the philosophical foundations of digital minimalism, starting with an examination of the forces that are making so many people’s digital lives increasingly intolerable, before moving on to a detailed discussion of the digital minimalism philosophy.
ex.t: 在第一部分中，我阐述了数字极简主义的哲学基础，首先审视了使许多人的数字生活日益难以忍受的各种力量，然后详细讨论了数字极简主义哲学。

ex.s: Part one concludes by introducing my suggested method for adopting this philosophy: the digital declutter.
ex.t: 第一部分最后介绍了我建议的践行这一理念的方法：数字清理。

ex.s: At the end of the thirty days, you will then add back a small number of carefully chosen online activities that you believe will provide massive benefits to the things you value.
ex.t: 三十天结束时，你再重新加入少量经过精心挑选的线上活动，即那些你认为能为你所珍视的事情带来巨大益处的活动。

ex.s: In the final chapter of part one, I’ll guide you through carrying out your own digital declutter.
ex.t: 在第一部分的最后一章，我将指导你完成自己的数字清理。

ex.s: Each chapter concludes with a collection of practices, which are designed to help you act on the big ideas of the chapter.
ex.t: 每一章都以一组实践练习结尾，这些练习旨在帮助你把本章的重要观点付诸行动。

ex.s: On March 7, 1907, the English statistician Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the “wisdom of crowds” effect.
ex.t: 1907年3月7日，英国统计学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿发表了一篇论文，阐述了后来被称为“群体智慧”效应的现象。

ex.s: The experiment of estimation he conducted showed that in some cases, the average of a large number of independent estimates could be quite accurate.
ex.t: 他进行的估算实验表明，在某些情况下，大量独立估算的平均值可以相当准确。

ex.s: This effect capitalizes on the fact that when people make errors, those errors aren’t always the same.
ex.t: 这种效应利用了这样一个事实：当人们犯错时，这些错误并不总是相同的。

ex.s: If people are similar and tend to make the same errors, then their errors won’t cancel each other out.
ex.t: 如果人们彼此相似并倾向于犯同样的错误，那么他们的错误就不会相互抵消。

ex.s: In more technical terms, the wisdom of crowds requires that people’s estimates be independent.
ex.t: 用更专业的术语来说，群体智慧要求人们的估算相互独立。

ex.s: If for whatever reasons, people’s errors become correlated or dependent, the accuracy of the estimate will go down.
ex.t: 如果由于某种原因，人们的错误变得相互关联或相互依赖，估算的准确性就会下降。

ex.s: The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals.
ex.t: 该研究的关键发现是：当人群被进一步分成可以进行讨论的小组时，这些小组的平均值比同等数量的独立个体的平均值更准确。

ex.s: For instance, the average obtained from the estimates of four discussion groups of five was significantly more accurate than the average obtained from 20 independent individuals.
ex.t: 例如，由四个五人讨论小组得出的平均估算值，明显比由20个独立个体得出的平均值更准确。

ex.s: In a follow-up study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group members actually did in their discussion.
ex.t: 在一项有100名大学生参加的后续研究中，研究人员试图更好地了解小组成员在讨论中实际做了什么。

ex.s: This happened some of the time, but it wasn’t the dominant response.
ex.t: 这种情况时有发生，但并不是主流反应。

ex.s: Most frequently, the groups reported that they “shared arguments and reasoned together.” Somehow, these arguments and reasoning resulted in a global reduction in error.
ex.t: 最常见的是，各小组报告说他们“分享论点并一起推理”。不知何故，这些论点和推理使错误总体上减少了。

ex.s: Although the studies led by Navajas have limitations and many questions remain the potential implications for group discussion and decision-making are enormous.
ex.t: 尽管纳瓦哈斯主导的研究存在局限性且仍有许多问题未解决，但其对小组讨论和决策的潜在影响是巨大的。

ex.s: “They come to us thinking vegetables are awful, dirt is awful, insects are awful.” Though some are initially scared of the insects and turned off by the dirt, most are eager to try something new.
ex.t: “他们来找我们时，认为蔬菜很讨厌，泥土很讨厌，昆虫很讨厌。”虽然有些人一开始害怕昆虫、厌恶泥土，但大多数人都渴望尝试新事物。

ex.s: Urban Sprouts’ classes, at two middle schools and two high schools, include hands-on experiments such as soil testing, flower-and-seed dissection, tastings of fresh or dried produce, and work in the garden.
ex.t: “城市萌芽”的课程在两所初中和两所高中开设，内容包括动手实验，如土壤检测、花和种子的解剖、品尝新鲜或晒干的农产品，以及在菜园里劳动。

ex.s: Several times a year, students cook the vegetables they grow, and they occasionally make salads for their entire schools.
ex.t: 每年有几次，学生们会烹饪自己种的蔬菜，偶尔还会为全校制作沙拉。

ex.s: Program evaluations show that kids eat more vegetables as a result of the classes.
ex.t: 项目评估显示，由于这些课程，孩子们吃了更多的蔬菜。

ex.s: She adds that the program’s benefits go beyond nutrition.
ex.t: 她补充说，这个项目的好处不止于营养。

ex.s: Besides, working in the garden seems to have a calming effect on Jaramillo’s special education students, many of whom have emotional control issues.
ex.t: 此外，在菜园里劳动似乎对哈拉米略的特殊教育学生有镇静作用，他们中许多人有情绪控制问题。

ex.s: Reading Art: Art for Book Lovers is a celebration of an everyday object — the book, represented here in almost three hundred artworks from museums around the world.
ex.t: 《阅读的艺术：爱书人的艺术》是对一种日常物品——书的礼赞，书中汇集了近三百件来自世界各地博物馆的艺术作品来呈现它。

ex.s: The image of the reader appears throughout history, in art made long before books as we now know them came into being.
ex.t: 读者的形象贯穿整个历史，出现在远早于我们今天所熟知的书籍诞生之前的艺术作品中。

ex.s: We see scenes of children learning to read at home or at school, with the book as a focus for relations between the generations.
ex.t: 我们看到孩子们在家中或学校学习阅读的场景，书本成为几代人之间关系的焦点。

ex.s: Before the wide use of the printing press, books were treasured objects and could be works of art in their own right.
ex.t: 在印刷术广泛使用之前，书籍是珍贵的物品，其本身就可以是艺术品。

ex.s: More recently, as books have become inexpensive or even throwaway, artists have used them as the raw material for artworks — transforming covers, pages or even complete volumes into paintings and sculptures.
ex.t: 更近一些时候，随着书籍变得廉价甚至可以随意丢弃，艺术家们开始把它们用作艺术品的原材料——把封面、书页甚至整册书变成绘画和雕塑。

ex.s: Continued developments in communication technologies were once believed to make the printed page outdated.
ex.t: 通信技术的不断发展曾让人们以为印刷书页将会过时。

ex.s: From a 21st-century point of view, the printed book is certainly ancient, but it remains as interactive as any battery-powered e-reader.
ex.t: 从21世纪的视角看，印刷书当然古老，但它与任何电池供电的电子阅读器一样具有互动性。

ex.s: To serve its function, a book must be activated by a user: the cover opened, the pages parted, the contents reviewed, perhaps notes written down or words underlined.
ex.t: 为了发挥其功能，一本书必须由使用者来激活：打开封面，翻开书页，浏览内容，也许还要写下笔记或划出字句。

ex.s: And in contrast to our increasingly networked lives where the information we consume is monitored and tracked, a printed book still offers the chance of a wholly private, “off-line” activity.
ex.t: 而且，与我们日益网络化的生活——我们所消费的信息受到监控和追踪——形成对比的是，印刷书仍然提供了一种完全私密的、“离线”活动的机会。

ex.s: The research team focused on a large urban park.
ex.t: 研究团队聚焦于一大型城市公园。

ex.s: They surveyed several hundred park-goers, asking them to submit a written summary online of a meaningful interaction they had with nature in the park.
ex.t: 他们调查了数百名游园者，请他们在线提交一份书面小结，描述他们在公园中与自然进行的一次有意义的互动。

ex.s: For example, one participant’s experience of “We sat and listened to the waves at the beach for a while” was assigned the categories “sitting at beach” and “listening to waves.”
ex.t: 例如，一位参与者的经历“我们在海滩上坐着听了一会儿海浪”被归入“坐在海滩上”和“听海浪”两个类别。

ex.s: Across the 320 submissions, a pattern of categories the researchers call a “nature language” began to emerge.
ex.t: 在320份提交材料中，一种被研究人员称为“自然语言”的类别模式开始显现。

ex.s: After the coding of all submissions, half a dozen categories were noted most often as important to visitors.
ex.t: 对所有提交材料进行编码后，有六种类别最常被游客提及为重要。

ex.s: These include encountering wildlife, walking along the edge of water, and following an established trail.
ex.t: 这些类别包括遇见野生动物、沿着水边散步，以及沿着既有的小径行走。

ex.s: Naming each nature experience creates a usable language, which helps people recognize and take part in the activities that are most satisfying and meaningful to them.
ex.t: 为每种自然体验命名创造出一种可用的语言，帮助人们认识并参与那些对他们来说最令人满足、最有意义的活动。

ex.s: For example, the experience of walking along the edge of water might be satisfying for a young professional on a weekend hike in the park.
ex.t: 例如，沿着水边散步的体验，对一位周末在公园里徒步的年轻职场人士来说可能很令人满足。

ex.s: “We’re trying to generate a language that helps bring the human-nature interactions back into our daily lives.
ex.t: “我们正试图创造一种语言，帮助把人与自然的互动带回我们的日常生活。

ex.s: And for that to happen, we also need to protect nature so that we can interact with it,” said Peter Kahn, a senior author of the study.
ex.t: 要做到这一点，我们还需要保护自然，这样我们才能与它互动，”该研究的资深作者彼得·卡恩说。

ex.s: What phenomenon does the author describe at the beginning of the text?
ex.t: 作者在文章开头描述了什么现象？

ex.t: 研究人员为什么把参与者的提交材料编码分类？

ex.s: To explain why the park attracts tourists.
ex.t: 为了解释公园吸引游客的原因。

ex.s: To analyze the main features of the park.
ex.t: 为了分析公园的主要特征。

ex.s: To find patterns in the visitors’ summaries.
ex.t: 为了从游客的小结中找出规律。

ex.s: What can we learn from the example given in paragraph 5?
ex.t: 从第五段给出的例子中我们可以了解到什么？

ex.t: 散步是接触自然的最好方式。

ex.s: The same nature experience takes different forms.
ex.t: 同一种自然体验可以有不同的形式。

ex.s: Whenever I tell people that I teach English at the Berlin Zoo, I almost always get a questioning look.
ex.t: 每当我告诉别人我在柏林动物园教英语时，几乎总会得到疑惑的眼神。

ex.s: Behind it, the person is trying to figure out who exactly I teach…the animals?
ex.t: 在那眼神背后，对方是在努力弄清楚我到底教谁……教动物吗？

ex.s: Since June 2017, right before the ___56___ (arrive) of the two new pandas, Meng Meng and Jiao Qing, I have been helping the panda keepers at the zoo to feel more comfortable and ___57___ (confidence) speaking English.
ex.t: 自2017年6月起，就在两只新熊猫梦梦和娇庆___56___（arrive）到来之前，我一直在帮助动物园的熊猫饲养员更轻松、更___57___（confidence）自信地说英语。

ex.t: 不是熊猫，尽管___59___用于医疗训练指令的语言实际上是英语。

ex.s: They talk to the flood of international tourists and to ___60___ (visit) Chinese zookeepers who often come to check on the pandas, which are on loan from China.
ex.t: 他们与蜂拥而至的国际游客交流，也与经常前来查看这些从中国租借的熊猫的___60___（visit）来访的中国饲养员交流。

ex.t: 能见证熊猫项目的发展___64___并看到熊猫们在新家安顿下来，我深感荣幸。

ex.s: Now, I’m living out that dream indirectly by helping the panda keepers do their job in English.
ex.t: 现在，我通过帮助熊猫饲养员用英语开展工作，间接实现了那个梦想。

ex.s: Writing was so difficult and painful for me that my teacher had allowed me to present my paper on the sinking of the Titanic by acting out a play, where I played all the parts.
ex.t: 写作对我来说太困难、太痛苦了，以至于老师允许我用表演戏剧的方式来呈现我关于泰坦尼克号沉没的论文，由我扮演所有角色。

ex.s: My story would come straight from the horse’s mouth.
ex.t: 我的故事将直接出自马之口。

ex.t: 那匹马在黑夜中疾驰时会想些什么呢？

ex.s: I checked out a half dozen books on Paul Revere from the library.
ex.t: 我从图书馆借了六本关于保罗·里维尔的书。

ex.s: When I handed in the essay to my teacher, he read it, laughed out loud, and said, “Great.
ex.t: 当我把文章交给老师时，他读了之后放声大笑，说：“很好。

ex.s: When I finally finished it, the thought of winning had given way to the enjoyment of writing.
ex.t: 当我终于完成时，获胜的念头已经让位于写作的乐趣。

ex.t: 它是唯一一家跻身全球50家最佳餐厅榜单前十的泰国餐厅。

ex.s: Head Chef David Thompson, who received a Michelin star for his Loodon-based Thai restaurant of the same name, opened this branch in the Metropolitan Hotel in 2010.
ex.t: 主厨大卫·汤普森曾凭借其位于伦敦的同名泰国餐厅获得米其林一星，他于2010年在大都会酒店开设了这家分店。

ex.t: 这座美丽的殖民风格宅邸里的菜单包括传统泰国菜与现代烹饪方法的结合。

ex.s: Serving hard-to-find Thai dishes in an elegant atmosphere, the restaurant is true to Thai cuisine’s roots, yet still manages to add a special twist.
ex.t: 这家餐厅在优雅的氛围中供应难得一见的泰国菜肴，忠实于泰国菜的根源，同时又不失独特的创新。

ex.s: The best table in this two-story colonial Thai home offers a window right into the kitchen, where you can see chef Gaggan and his staff in action.
ex.t: 在这栋两层泰式殖民风格住宅中，最好的座位正对着厨房的窗口，在那里你可以看到加根主厨和他的团队在忙碌。

ex.s: It shows the cooking process to guests.
ex.t: 它向客人展示烹饪过程。

ex.s: From the age of six, Terri, now 26, accompanied Derek to work during her school holidays.
ex.t: 从六岁起，现年26岁的特丽就在学校放假期间陪德里克去干活。

ex.s: With millions of people likely to take on DIY projects over that coming weeks, new research shows that more than half of people are planning to make the most of the long, warm summer days to get jobs done.
ex.t: 数以百万计的人可能在接下来的几周里动手做DIY项目，新的研究显示，超过一半的人打算利用漫长而温暖的夏日把活干完。

ex.t: 每个项目的平均花费约为823英镑。

ex.t: 五分之二的人希望提升自己房子的价值。

ex.s: Though DIY has traditionally been seen as male hobby, the research shows it is women now leading the charge.
ex.t: 尽管DIY传统上被视为男性的爱好，但研究显示，如今是女性冲在最前面。

ex.t: 特丽是如何避免被扣租房押金的？

ex.t: 这项研究显示了DIY的什么趋势？

ex.s: It was full of ideas that were new to me so I spent the summer with my head in and out of that book.
ex.t: 书里满是对我来说全新的思想，所以我整个夏天都沉浸在那本书里，时而读时而想。

ex.s: Nothing kills the love for philosophy faster than people who think they understand Foucault, Baudrillard, or Confucius better than you — and then try to explain them.
ex.t: 没有什么比那些自以为比你更懂福柯、波德里亚或孔子——然后还试图向你解释的人——更能扼杀对哲学的热爱了。

ex.s: Eric weiner’s The Socrates Express: In Search of Life Lessons from Dead Philosophers reawakened my love for philosophy.
ex.t: 埃里克·韦纳的《苏格拉底快车：从已故哲学家那里寻找人生课》重新点燃了我对哲学的热爱。

ex.s: The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche.
ex.t: 最终的阅读体验是：我们学会像苏格拉底那样好奇发问，像梭罗那样观察，像叔本华那样倾听，像尼采那样无怨无悔。

ex.s: He makes philosophical thought an appealing exercise that improves the quality of our experiences, and he does so with plenty of humor.
ex.t: 他把哲学思考变成一种有吸引力的练习，能提升我们体验的质量，而且他做得妙趣横生。

ex.s: The Socrates Express is a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity and gradually pulls them in deeper thoughts on desire, loneliness, and aging.

ex.s: Being at the right place at the right time is decisive in any style of photography.
ex.t: 在任何风格的摄影中，在对的时间出现在对的地点都是决定性的。

ex.s: I often leave early to seek the right destinations so I can set up early to avoid missing the moment I am attempting to photograph.
ex.t: 我经常早早出发去寻找合适的目的地，这样我可以提前架好设备，避免错过我想拍摄的瞬间。

ex.s: I have missed plenty of beautiful sunsets/sunrises due to being on the spot only five minutes before the best moment.
ex.t: 由于只在最佳时刻前五分钟赶到现场，我错过了许多美丽的日落和日出。

ex.s: After we found a crazy-looking road that hung over a bunch of rocks, we decided to photograph the scene at sunset.
ex.t: 在我们发现一条悬在一堆岩石上方、造型奇特的公路后，我们决定在日落时分拍摄这个场景。

ex.s: The position enabled us to look over the lake with the sunset in the background.

ex.s: We managed to leave this spot to climb higher because of the spare time until sunset.
ex.t: 由于距离日落还有空闲时间，我们设法离开这个地点爬到更高的地方。

ex.s: Once we found the place, it was stressful getting lights and cameras set up in the limited time.

ex.s: Still, looking back on the photos, they are some of my best shots though they could have been so much better if I would have been prepared and managed my time wisely.
ex.t: 尽管如此，回头看这些照片，它们仍是我最好的作品之一，不过如果我准备充分、合理安排时间，它们本可以好得多。

ex.s: If you want to tell the history of the whole world, a history that does not privilege one part of humanity, you cannot do it through texts alone, because only some of the world has ever had texts, while most of the world, for most of the time, has not.
ex.t: 如果你想讲述整个世界的历史，一部不偏袒任何一部分人类的历史，你就不能只依靠文字文献，因为世界上只有一部分地区曾经有过文字，而世界上大部分地区在大部分时间里都没有。

ex.s: The clearest example of this between literate and non-literate history is perhaps the first conflict, at Botany Bay, between Captain Cook’s voyage and the Australian Aboriginals.
ex.t: 在有文字和无文字历史之间，最清楚的例子也许是库克船长的航行与澳大利亚原住民在植物湾发生的第一次冲突。

ex.s: From the English side, we have scientific reports and the captain’s record of that terrible day.
ex.t: 从英方那里，我们有科学报告和船长对那可怕一天的记录。

ex.s: From the Australian side, we have only a wooden shield (盾) dropped by a man in flight after his first experience of gunshot.
ex.t: 从澳大利亚一方那里，我们只有一面木盾（盾），是一个人在第一次经历枪击后逃跑时丢下的。

ex.s: If we want to reconstruct what was actually going on that day, the shield must be questioned and interpreted as deeply and strictly as the written reports.
ex.t: 如果我们想还原那天实际发生的事情，就必须像对待文字报告一样，深入而严格地追问和解读这面盾。

ex.s: In addition to the problem of miscomprehension from both sides, there are victories accidentally or deliberately twisted, especially when only the victors know how to write.
ex.t: 除了双方相互误解的问题之外，还有一些胜利被无意或有意地歪曲，尤其是当只有胜利者懂得书写的时候。

ex.s: Those who are on the losing side often have only their things to tell their stories.
ex.t: 处于失败一方的人往往只能用他们的物品来讲述自己的故事。

ex.s: The Caribbean Taino, the Australian Aboriginals, the African people of Benin and the Incas, all of whom appear in this book, can speak to us now of their past achievements most powerfully through the objects they made: a history told through things gives them back a voice.
ex.t: 加勒比海的泰诺人、澳大利亚原住民、贝宁的非洲人和印加人——他们都出现在本书中——如今可以通过他们制作的物品最有力地向我们讲述他们过去的成就：一部通过实物讲述的历史把声音还给了他们。

ex.s: If we are to find the other half of that conversation, we have to read not just the texts, but the objects.
ex.t: 如果我们要找到那场对话的另一半，我们就不仅要读文字，还要读实物。

ex.s: As Kristian Hammond, professor of electrical engineering and computer science at Northwestern University, put it: “There’s never a stage at which the system knows what it’s talking about.”
ex.t: 正如西北大学电气工程和计算机科学教授克里斯蒂安·哈蒙德所说："系统从来没有一个阶段知道自己谈论的是什么。"

ex.s: What Hammond is referring to is the question of meaning and meaning is central to what distinguishes the least intelligent of humans from the most intelligent of machines.
ex.t: 哈蒙德指的是意义问题，而意义是将最不聪明的人类与最聪明的机器区分开来的核心所在。

ex.s: What matters is not just the outside of a string of symbols, but the inside too, not just how they are arranged but what they mean.
ex.t: 重要的不仅是符号串的外表，还有内在；不仅是它们的排列方式，还有它们的含义。

ex.s: Meaning emerges through a process of social interaction, not of computation, interaction that shapes the content of the symbols in our heads.
ex.t: 意义通过社会互动的过程产生，而非计算过程——这种互动塑造了我们头脑中符号的内容。

ex.s: The rules that assign meaning lie not just inside our heads, but also outside, in society, in social memory, social conventions and social relations.
ex.t: 赋予意义的规则不仅存在于我们头脑内部，也存在于外部——在社会中，在社会记忆、社会惯例和社会关系中。

ex.s: “Solar projects need to be good neighbors,” says Jordan Macknick, the head of the Innovative Site Preparation and Impact Reductions on the Environment(InSPIRE)project.
ex.t: "太阳能项目需要做好邻居，"创新场地准备与环境影响力减损（InSPIRE）项目负责人乔丹·麦克尼克说。

ex.s: “They need to be protectors of the land and contribute to the agricultural economy.” InSPIRE is investigating practical approaches to “low-impact” solar development, which focuses on establishing and operating solar farms in a way that is kinder to the land.
ex.t: "它们需要成为土地的保护者并为农业经济做贡献。"InSPIRE正在研究"低影响"太阳能开发的实用方法，重点关注以一种对土地更友好的方式建立和运营太阳能农场。

ex.s: Habitat loss, pesticide use, and climate change have caused dramatic declines in pollinator populations over the past couple of decades, which has damaged the US agricultural economy.

ex.t: 我一把她抱起来，她就停止了挣扎。

ex.t: 我塞了一块布堵住洞口，带着她走到外面，随手关好了门。

ex.s: When I opened my hand, the bird did not fly away; she sat looking at me with her bright eyes.

ex.t: 三元组合的第一部分是感觉运动。

ex.s: The third part is meaning-knowledge.
ex.t: 第三部分是意义知识。

ex.s: Art is deeply personal, because when two people see the same artwork, our perception can create vastly different experiences of meaning.
ex.t: 艺术是非常个人的，因为当两个人看到同一件艺术品时，我们的感知可以创造出截然不同的意义体验。

ex.s: We also get enjoyment from the knowledge of how something was made.

ex.s: Informed by neuroaesthetics, the next time I create my art I will value the process even more, enjoying the activation of the aesthetic triad in my brain as I admire the vivid images that I have created.
ex.t: 受神经美学的启发，下次创作艺术时，我将更加重视创作过程，在欣赏我创造的生动图像的同时，享受大脑审美三元组的激活。

ex.s: One of them is about how the most accessible information in the present affects decisions about the future.
ex.t: 其中之一是关于当前最容易获取的信息如何影响对未来做出的决策。

ex.s: Indeed, when it comes to environmental transformations, we can develop a form of collective “poor memory”, and each new generation can believe the state of affairs they encounter is nothing out of the ordinary.
ex.t: 事实上，在环境变化方面，我们可以形成一种集体的"糟糕记忆"，每一代新人都可以认为他们遇到的状况没有什么不寻常的。

ex.s: Children, on the other hand, have no idea that insect population has dropped dramatically.
ex.t: 另一方面，孩子们根本不知道昆虫数量已经大幅下降。

ex.s: The human mind is bad at noting slow change.
ex.t: 人类大脑不善于察觉缓慢的变化。

ex.s: What does the author intend to tell us?
ex.t: 谦逊应是人类进步的动力。

ex.s: D Bias towards the present helps reduce near-term desires.
ex.t: D 对当前的偏见有助于减少近期的欲望。

ex.s: The reason is simple: we know of just one type of life and it’s challenging to do science with a sample size of one.
ex.t: 原因很简单：我们只知道一种生命形式，而仅凭一个样本做科学是很有挑战性的。

ex.s: The field of artificial life-called ALife for short — is the systematic attempt to spell out life’s fundamental principles.
ex.t: 人工生命领域——简称ALife——是系统性地阐明生命基本原理的尝试。

ex.s: Many of these practitioners, so-called ALifers, think that somehow making life is the surest way to really understand what life is.
ex.t: 这些从业者中的许多——所谓的ALife研究者——认为，以某种方式创造生命是真正理解生命的最佳途径。

ex.s: This track record makes ALife a ripe target for criticism, such as declarations of the field’s doubtful scientific value.
ex.t: 这使得ALife成为批评的有力目标，例如对该领域科学价值的质疑。

ex.s: Asking about “the point” of ALife might be, well, missing the point entirely, he says.
ex.t: 询问ALife的"意义"可能——嗯——完全偏离了重点，他说。

ex.s: “The existence of a living system is not about the use of anything.” Alan says.
ex.t: "一个活系统的存在不是为了使用任何东西。"艾伦说。

ex.s: “Some people ask me, ‘So what’s the worth of artificial life?’ Do you ever think, ‘What is the worth of your grandmother?’”
ex.t: "有人问我，'那人工生命有什么价值？'你有没有想过，'你祖母的价值是什么？'"

ex.s: As much as many ALifers hate emphasizing their research’s applications, the attempts to create artificial life could have practical payoffs.
ex.t: 尽管许多ALife研究者不喜欢强调他们研究的实际应用，但创造人工生命的尝试可能会有实际的回报。

ex.s: This is the capacity for a system to create essentially endless complexity, to be a sort of “novelty generator”.
ex.t: 这是一个系统创造本质上无限复杂性的能力，成为一种"新颖性生成器"。

ex.s: The only system known to exhibit this is Earth’s biosphere.
ex.t: 已知唯一能展示这种能力的系统是地球的生物圈。

ex.s: If the field of ALife manages to reproduce life’s endless “creativity” in some virtual model, those same principles could give rise to truly inventive machines.
ex.t: 如果ALife领域能够在某些虚拟模型中复制生命无限的"创造力"，那么同样的原理可能会催生真正具有创造力的机器。

ex.s: Compared with the developments of Al, advances in ALife are harder to recognize.
ex.t: 与人工智能的发展相比，ALife的进展更难被识别。

ex.s: One reason is that ALife is a field in which the central concept — life itself — is undefined.
ex.t: 原因之一是ALife是一个核心概念——生命本身——尚未被定义的领域。

ex.s: The lack of agreement among ALifers doesn’t help either.
ex.t: ALife研究者之间的缺乏共识也无济于事。

ex.s: The result is a diverse line of projects that each advance along their unique paths.
ex.t: 结果是形成了多样化的项目系列，每个项目都沿着各自独特的路径前进。

ex.s: For better or worse, ALife mirrors the very subject it studies.
ex.t: 无论好坏，ALife反映了它所研究的对象本身。

ex.s: But even this dismissal suggests something：perhaps, just like life itself throughout the universe, the rise of ALife will prove unavoidable.
ex.t: 但即使是这种否定也暗示着某种东西：也许就像宇宙中的生命本身一样，ALife的兴起将是不可避免的。

ex.s: In a world where nearly 800 million people a year go hungry, “food waste goes against the moral grain,” as Elizabeth Royte writes in this month’s cover story.
ex.t: 在一个每年有近8亿人口挨饿的世界里，"食物浪费违背道德准则"，正如Elizabeth Royte在本月封面故事中所写的那样。

ex.s: Producing food that no one eats wastes the water, fuel, and other resources used to grow it.
ex.t: 生产没人吃的食物浪费了种植它所用的水、燃料和其他资源。

ex.s: In fact, Royte writes, “if food waste were a country, it would be the third largest producer of greenhouse gases in the world.”
ex.t: 事实上，Royte写道，"如果食物浪费是一个国家，它将是世界上第三大温室气体排放国。"

ex.s: Human speech contains more than 2,000 different sounds, from the common “m” and “a” to the rare clicks of some southern African languages.
ex.t: 人类语音包含2000多种不同的声音，从常见的"m"和"a"到某些南部非洲语言中罕见的咔嗒声。

ex.s: A ground-breaking, five-year study shows that diet-related changes in human bite led to new speech sounds that are now found in half the world’s languages.
ex.t: 一项开创性的五年研究表明，与饮食相关的人类咬合变化导致了现在世界一半语言中都存在的新的语音。

ex.s: More than 30 years ago, the scholar Charles Hockett noted that speech sounds called labiodentals, such as “f” and “v”, were more common in the languages of societies that ate softer foods.
ex.t: 30多年前，学者Charles Hockett注意到，被称为唇齿音的语音（如"f"和"v"）在饮食较软的社会的语言中更为常见。

ex.s: Now a team of researchers led by Damián Blasi at the University of Zurich, Switzerland, has found how and why this trend arose.
ex.t: 现在，由苏黎世大学的Damián Blasi领导的研究团队发现了这种趋势是如何以及为何产生的。

ex.s: The team showed that this change in bite was connected with the development of agriculture in the Neolithic period.
ex.t: 团队表明，这种咬合变化与新石器时代农业的发展有关。

ex.s: The jawbone didn’t have to do as much work and so didn’t grow to be so large.
ex.t: 颌骨不必那么用力，所以长得没那么大了。

ex.s: Analyses of a language database also confirmed that there was a global change in the sound of world languages after the Neolithic age, with the use of “f” and “v” increasing remarkably during the last few thousand years.
ex.t: 对语言数据库的分析也证实，新石器时代之后世界语言的声音发生了全球性变化，"f"和"v"的使用在过去几千年中显著增加。

ex.s: These sounds are still not found in the languages of many hunter-gatherer people today.
ex.t: 这些声音在今天许多狩猎采集民族的语言中仍然不存在。

ex.s: This research overturns the popular view that all human speech sounds were present when human beings evolved around 300,000 years ago. ”The set of speech sounds we use has not necessarily remained stable since the appearance of human beings, but rather the huge variety of speech sounds that we find today is the product of a complex interplay of things like biological change and cultural evolution,“ said Steven Moran, a member of the research team.
ex.t: 这项研究推翻了人类在大约30万年前进化时所有语音就已经存在的流行观点。"我们使用的语音集合自人类出现以来不一定保持稳定，相反，我们今天发现的巨大语音多样性是生物变化和文化进化等复杂相互作用的结果，"研究团队成员Steven Moran说。

ex.s: The second group did high-intensity aerobic exercise under the guidance of a trainer for four or more days a week.

ex.s: "The sweet spot in life to start exercising, if you haven't already, is in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility," Levine says.
ex.t: "如果你还没有开始运动，生命中开始运动的最佳时期是中年晚期，这时心脏仍有弹性，"Levine说。

ex.t: 她们当时为什么要去呢？

ex.s: They could do precisely the same thing to inspect railway lines and other vital aspects of rail infrastructure such as the correct position of railway tracks and switching points.
ex.t: 检查越频繁，铁路的安全性、可靠性和准点率就会越高。

ex.s: The more regularly they can be inspected, the more railway safety, reliability and on-time performance will be improved.
ex.t: 这包括节省大量的维护成本和更好地保护铁路人员的安全。

ex.s: It is calculated that European railways alone spend approximately 20 billion euros a year on maintenance, including sending maintenance staff, often at night, to inspect and repair the rail infrastructure.
ex.t: 这可能是危险的工作，如果有无人机协助工作人员就可以避免这种危险。

ex.s: That can be dangerous work that could be avoided with drones assisting the crews’ efforts.
ex.t: 通过使用最新技术，无人机还可以开始为铁路提供更高价值的服务，在铁轨或道岔造成安全问题之前检测故障。

ex.s: By using the latest technologies, drones could also start providing higher-value services for railways, detecting faults in the rail or switches, before they can cause any safety problems.
ex.t: 为了执行这些任务，铁路无人机不需要在空中飞行。

ex.s: Engineers are now working on a new concept: the rail drones of the future.
ex.t: 它们将在列车前方轨道上运行，并被编程为自主运行。

ex.s: They will be moving on the track ahead of the train, and programmed to run autonomously.

ex.s: Very small drones with advanced sensors and AI and travelling ahead of the train could guide it like a co-pilot.
ex.t: 凭借其预见能力，它们可以发出任何问题的信号，使高速列车能够及时做出反应。

ex.t: 政府对软饮料征收的糖税带来的收入只有部长最初预测的一半，这是该政策的首次官方数据所显示的。

ex.s: The Government's sugar tax on soft drinks has brought in half as much money as Ministers first predicted it would generate, the first official data on the policy has shown.
ex.t: 据信今天的儿童和青少年摄入的糖分是推荐水平的三倍，使他们面临更高的患病风险。

ex.s: It is believed that today's children and teenagers are consuming three times the recommended level of sugar, putting them at a higher risk of the disease.
ex.t: 最初糖税预计每年为国库带来5.2亿英镑收入。

ex.s: Initially the sugar tax was expected to make £520m a year for the Treasury.
ex.t: 然而，前六个月的数据显示收入将不到这个数字的一半。

ex.s: However, data of the first six months showed it would make less than half this amount.
ex.t: 目前预计截至2019年4月的财年将产生2.4亿英镑收入，这笔钱将用于学校体育。

ex.s: At present it is expected to generate £240m for the year ending in April 2019, which will go to school sports.
ex.t: 根据国库数据，由于制造商为了避免收费所做的努力，饮料中的糖减少了4500万公斤。

ex.s: Drinks now contain 45 million fewer kilos of sugar as a result of manufacturers' efforts to avoid the charge, according to Treasury figures.
ex.t: 自4月以来，饮料公司必须根据含糖量为他们生产或进口的每升含糖饮料支付18至24便士。

ex.s: The United States rose to global power on the strength of its technology, and the lifeblood that technology has long been electricity.

ex.s: The story begins in the last years of the 18th century in Scotland, where Watt perfected "the machine that changed the world".

ex.s: Meanwhile, over the course of 19th century, electricity went from mere curiosity to a basic necessity.

ex.s: I often had to be an interpreter for the Italian-speaking ones.
ex.t: 我经常必须为那些说意大利语的人充当翻译。

ex.s: As I served the role of vital communication link, I was reminded of my desperate struggle to converse before I learned English.
ex.t: 当我担任重要沟通纽带的角色时，我想起了我在学会英语之前那种拼命想交流的挣扎。

ex.s: I watched with great sympathy as elderly Italians tried to hold a conversation in Italian with people who did not speak the language.
ex.t: 我怀着极大的同情看着年长的意大利人努力用意大利语和不懂这门语言的人交谈。

ex.s: This work expanded my mind in ways that are impossible inside the four walls of a classroom.
ex.t: 这项工作以不可能在教室四面墙内实现的方式开阔了我的思维。

ex.s: Walking through the streets of Brooklyn today, I am no longer confused by this city’s sounds and smells.
ex.t: 今天走在布鲁克林的街道上，我不再对这个城市的声音和气味感到困惑。

ex.s: What did the author realize after entering school in Brooklyn?
ex.t: 作者进入布鲁克林的学校后意识到了什么？

ex.s: The food was terrible.
ex.t: 食物很难吃。

ex.s: Who does “the little girl” in paragraph 2 refer to?
ex.t: 第2段中的"小女孩"指的是谁？

ex.s: The author herself.
ex.t: 作者本人。

ex.s: The author’s classmate.
ex.t: 作者的同学。

ex.s: How did the summer job benefit the author?
ex.t: 暑期工作给作者带来了什么好处？

ex.s: It opened her eyes to the real world.
ex.t: 让她看到了真实的世界。

ex.s: All around the world, there are small changes taking place.
ex.t: 全世界各地都在发生着微小的变化。

ex.s: At the side of roads, behind school playgrounds and on all kinds of unloved pieces of land across towns and cities, tiny forests barely the size of tennis courts are appearing, making a great place for both wildlife and local people who may not normally have easy access to nature.
ex.t: 在路边、学校操场后面以及城镇和城市中各种无人问津的土地上，只有网球场地大小的小森林正在出现，为野生动物和通常不容易接触到大自然的当地居民创造了一个绝佳场所。

ex.s: This is the Tiny Forest movement, which aims to prove that the best things in life really do come in small packages.
ex.t: 这就是微型森林运动，旨在证明生活中最好的东西确实来自小包装。

ex.s: Tiny forests were first pioneered as a concept in the 1970s by Dr Miyawaki, a Japanese botanist.
ex.t: 微型森林的概念最早由日本植物学家宫胁博士在20世纪70年代开创。

ex.s: As he went on to share his concept with others, the idea soon took off in India and other countries before eventually reaching Europe, where it became popular in places like France, Belgium and the Netherlands.
ex.t: 当他与其他人分享他的概念时，这个想法很快在印度和其他国家流行起来，最终传到欧洲，在法国、比利时和荷兰等地受欢迎。

ex.s: Louise Hartley, who is leading the Tiny Forest project in the UK, explains that the process begins by identifying areas in which a tiny forest could have the biggest influence.
ex.t: Louise Hartley是英国微型森林项目的负责人，她解释说这个过程首先确定微型森林可能产生最大影响的区域。

ex.s: “We see it as a chance to try to break the growing disconnect between people and nature.”
ex.t: "我们把这视为尝试打破人与自然之间日益增长隔阂的机会。"

ex.s: This variety, coupled with the fact that tiny forests grow up to ten times faster than standard forests, means they attract a rich abundance of wildlife.
ex.t: 这种多样性加上微型森林的生长速度比标准森林快多达十倍这一事实，意味着它们吸引了丰富的野生动物。

ex.s: It’s also thought that these places could help reduce the risk of flooding, remove carbon from the atmosphere and fight climate change, as well as improving the mental health of those living locally.
ex.t: 人们还认为这些地方可以帮助减少洪水风险、从大气中去除碳、应对气候变化，以及改善当地居民的心理健康。

ex.s: What do we know about the Tiny Forest movement?
ex.t: 关于微型森林运动我们能了解到什么？

ex.s: It began in Europe in the 1970s.
ex.t: 它于20世纪70年代在欧洲开始。

ex.s: It will spread to the countryside.
ex.t: 它将扩展到农村地区。

ex.s: What is special about the trees in a Tiny Forest?
ex.t: 微型森林中的树木有什么特别之处？

ex.s: Subjects who practiced the language moderately beforehand made fewer errors than those who practiced extensively or not at all.
ex.t: 事先适度练习这种语言的人犯的错误比那些大量练习或根本不练习的人少。

ex.s: High levels of knowledge can make people too attached to traditional ways of viewing problems across fields the arts, sciences, and politics.
ex.t: 高水平的知识可能使人们过于固守各领域（艺术、科学和政治）传统的思维方式。

ex.s: How long we stay on the clock and how we spend that time are under careful examination in many workplaces.
ex.t: 我们在工作场所花费的时间和如何支配这些时间都受到仔细审视。

ex.s: The young banker who eats lunch at his desk is probably seen as a go-getter, while his colleagues who chat over a relaxed conference-room meal get dirty looks from the corner office.
ex.t: 在办公桌前吃午饭的年轻银行家可能被视为积极进取的人，而在轻松的会议室用餐聊天的同事却会受到角落办公室的白眼。

ex.s: “People from cultures that value relationships more than ours does are shocked by the thought of eating alone in front of a computer”, says Art Markman, a professor of psychology at the University of Texas, Austin.
ex.t: "来自比我们更重视人际关系的文化背景的人会对在电脑前独自吃饭的想法感到震惊，"德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校心理学教授Art Markman说。

ex.s: “Part of being a good thinker is experiencing things that are seemingly unrelated to what you are working on at the moment but give you fresh ideas about your work,” he says.
ex.t: "成为一个好的思考者的部分体验是那些看似与你当前工作无关但能给你的工作带来新灵感的事情，"他说。

ex.s: Moderate effort produces the best result.
ex.t: 适度的努力产生最好的结果。

ex.s: The underlined word “go-getter” in paragraph 3 refers to someone Who_______.
ex.t: 第3段中带下划线的单词"go-getter"指的是什么样的人？________。

ex.s: What can be inferred from the last paragraph?
ex.t: 从最后一段可以推断出什么？

ex.s: What does the text seem to advocate?
ex.t: 这篇文章似乎倡导什么？

ex.s: Harmony in the work environment.
ex.t: 工作环境的和谐。

ex.s: They were polite requests for the latest game or toy.
ex.t: 这些都是礼貌地请求最新的游戏或玩具。

ex.s: The very best communicators are those who know how to adjust their language to match their audience.
ex.t: 最好的沟通者是那些知道如何根据读者调整语言的人。

ex.s: The age of pen-and-paper letter writing may have passed.
ex.t: 纸笔写信的时代可能已经过去了。

ex.s: But if this is the only kind of writing young people do, it will cause problems.
ex.t: 但如果这是年轻人唯一做的写作类型，就会造成问题。

ex.s: Small children are easy to throw up in the air and catch-and they ____16____ it.
ex.t: 小孩子很容易被抛向空中再接住——他们也____16____喜欢这样做。

ex.s: “Again, Daddy, again!” Jacky shouts as I throw him skywards and catch him on the way back down again.
ex.t: "再来一次，爸爸！"当我把Jacky向上抛再接住时他喊道。

ex.s: His trust in me is ____19____ which is quite a nice feeling, but at the same time gives me a huge sense of ____20____ .
ex.t: 他对我的信任是____19____这感觉很好，但同时给了我巨大的____20____感。

ex.s: Every time I _____25_____ Jacky to something new, he’ll do it only because he trusts me and feels _____26_____ in the knowledge that he won’t get hurt ._____27_____ , teaching Jacky to swim means he has to _____28_____ that, when he’s swimming in the big pool, I’ll come to his rescue if his doggy paddle lets him down.
ex.t: 每次我_____25_____Jacky尝试新事物时，他这样做只是因为他信任我并且感到_____26_____确信他不会受伤。_____27_____，教Jacky游泳意味着他必须_____28____相信，当他在大泳池里游泳时，如果他的狗刨式划水不管用了，我会去救他。

ex.s: Through touch, the one thing gallery signs tell you not ____37____ (do).
ex.t: 通过触摸——画廊标识告诉你不要____37____ (do)做的唯一一件事。

ex.s: "The feeling of being able to see it _____45_____ to form my opinion is like breaking down another wall as a blind person.”
ex.t: "能够看到它并形成自己的观点的感觉_____45_____就像作为盲人打破了另一堵墙。"

ex.s: I thought that we would just be passing out dinners to those in need, but I found out we would be doing everything from preparing to serving the dinner.
ex.t: 我以为我们只是分发晚餐给那些需要帮助的人，但我发现我们要做的事情从准备到服务晚餐无所不包。

ex.s: We began preparing the food, from mixing salad dressing to separating frozen meat.
ex.t: 我们开始准备食物，从调制沙拉酱到分拣冷冻肉类。

ex.s: Much still needed to be done before dinner was served, but already outside the building many homeless people were gathering.
ex.t: 晚餐供应之前还有很多事情要做，但建筑物外面已经聚集了许多无家可归的人。

ex.s: It wasn’t until a couple of hours later that we opened the doors and began serving dinner.
ex.t: 直到几个小时后我们才开门开始分发晚餐。

ex.s: As the line of people came toward me, I got a little scared.
ex.t: 当人群朝我走来时，我有点害怕。

ex.s: I’d come face to face with the homeless: How should I act?
ex.t: 我将面对无家可归的人：我应该怎么做？

ex.s: While some of the people looked very friendly, some of them looked so dangerous.
ex.t: 虽然有些人看起来很友好，有些人看起来很危险。

ex.s: Some looked like they had tally given up on life, while others seemed to be making the best of the situation, smiling and joking.
ex.t: 有些人看起来已经彻底放弃了生活，而另一些人似乎在尽力适应现状，微笑着开玩笑。

ex.s: It saddened me to think of how many people there were who didn’t have a place to call home and the only food they got came from a soup kitchen.
ex.t: 想到有那么多人没有家可回，唯一的食物来源就是施粥所，我感到难过。

ex.s: One Monday morning, while the children were enjoying “free play”, I stepped to the doorway of the classroom to take a break.
ex.t: 一个周一早晨，当孩子们享受"自由游戏"时，我走到教室门口休息。

ex.s: Suddenly, I ____1____ a movement of the heavy wooden door.
ex.t: 突然，我注意到厚重的木门有动静。

ex.s: This was the very door I ____2____ guided the children through to ensure their safety from the bitter cold.
ex.t: 这正是那扇我____2____引导孩子们穿过以确保他们免受严寒侵袭的门。

ex.s: He had been dropped off at school late and was ____4____ to open the door.
ex.t: 他上学晚了，正在____4____努力开门。

ex.s: Without a word, I rushed him to the hospital.
ex.t: 二话不说，我赶紧把他送到了医院。

ex.s: He’d need time to ____5____ , and wouldn’t come for class the next day, I thought.
ex.t: 他需要时间____5____恢复，我想第二天他不会来上课了。

ex.s: The next morning, one of the first to ____6____ was my little frostbitten boy.
ex.t: 第二天早上，最先____6____到达的之一就是那个冻伤了的小男孩。

ex.s: His words have stayed with me all these years, “I knew you would open the door.”
ex.t: 他的话这些年一直伴随着我，"我知道你会打开门的。"

ex.s: Helen was walking down the street late ____11____ the evening, her arms filled with grocery bags.
ex.t: Helen深夜____11____走在街上，怀里抱着杂货袋。

ex.s: Focused on balancing the bags, she didn’t notice her wallet falling out of her pocket.
ex.t: 专注于保持袋子平衡，她没注意到钱包从口袋里掉了出来。

ex.s: Eventually, the man ____13____ (catch) up with her, and he was only trying to return her wallet!
ex.t: 最终，那个男人____13____ (catch)追上了她，他只是想把钱包还给她！

ex.s: However, a strong smell is added so that we can raise the alarm when we detect the smell associated with danger.
ex.t: 然而，添加了强烈的气味以便我们在检测到与危险相关的气味时能够发出警报。

ex.s: The use of those plastics ____20____ (increase) by 300% since 2019.
ex.t: 自2019年以来，这些塑料的使用量____20____ (increase)增加了300%。

ex.s: The world won’t survive if this situation continues.
ex.t: 如果这种情况继续下去，世界将无法承受。

ex.s: It’s an opportunity to deepen your understanding of the key points from lecture materials while you are applying your skills to solve problems.
ex.t: 这是一个在你运用技能解决问题的同时加深你对讲座材料关键点的理解的机会。

ex.s: If a session is full, you can register for the waiting list.
ex.t: 如果课程已满，你可以注册候补名单。

ex.s: When you are placed on a waiting list, we will email you a number which tells you where you are on the list.
ex.t: 当你被列入候补名单时，我们会发邮件给你一个号码，告诉你在名单上的位置。

ex.s: If you are close to the front of the list, you have a good chance of gaining a place in the programme in the near future.
ex.t: 如果你接近名单前列，你在不久的将来很有可能获得项目名额。

ex.s: If you miss two PASS sessions in a row, you will be deregistered and your place will be given to someone on the waiting list.
ex.t: 如果你连续错过两次PASS课程，你将被取消注册，你的位置将给候补名单上的人。

ex.s: Make sure you fill in the attendance sheet at each session to record your attendance.
ex.t: 确保每次课程都填写考勤表以记录出勤情况。

ex.s: If you believe you have received the email in error, email the PASS office at  passoffice@umbs. edu..
ex.t: 如果你认为收到邮件有误，请发邮件至passoffice@umbs.edu..

ex.s: Fill in the attendance sheet.
ex.t: 填写出勤表。

ex.s: Sign up for the waiting list.
ex.t: 注册候补名单。

ex.s: Email the office their numbers on the list.
ex.t: 发邮件给办公室他们在名单上的号码。

ex.s: My perfectionist tendencies were the main root of this: I wanted to be perfect at whatever I did, which obviously in life is not possible, but it consumed me.
ex.t: 我的完美主义倾向是主要原因：我想在所做的任何事情上都做到完美，这在生活中显然是不可能的，但它吞噬了我。

ex.s: His presentation not only awed and inspired me, but also helped emerge an inner desire to make a difference in the world.
ex.t: 他的演讲不仅让我惊叹和受到启发，还激发了我内心想要在这个世界做出改变的愿望。

ex.s: A month later, Brown invited me to attend the World Youth Wildlife Conference.
ex.t: 一个月后，Brown邀请我参加世界青年野生动物大会。

ex.s: Looking back, I now see that this would be the first in a series of timely opportunities that my old self would have let pass, but that this new and more confident Alice enthusiastically seized.
ex.t: 回顾往事，我现在明白这将是第一个及时机会，旧的我可能会让它溜走，而这个新的、更自信的Alice热情地抓住了。

ex.s: Shortly after I received his invitation, applications to join the Youth for Nature and the Youth for Planet groups were sent around through my high school.
ex.t: 收到他的邀请后不久，申请加入自然青年和地球青年团体的表格通过我的高中发放了出来。

ex.s: I decided to commit to completing the applications, and soon I was a part of a growing global team of young people working to protect nature.
ex.t: 我决定致力于完成申请，很快我就成为了一个不断壮大的全球青年保护自然团队的一员。

ex.s: It was that voice in the back of my head telling me that one phrase that has stopped so many people from reaching their potential: I can’t.
ex.t: 正是我脑海中的那个声音告诉我那个阻止许多人发挥潜力的短语：我不行。

ex.s: What was the main cause for Alice’s anxiety?
ex.t: Alice焦虑的主要原因是什么？

ex.s: She tasted the sweetness of friendship.
ex.t: 她尝到了友谊的甜蜜。

ex.s: She learned about the harm of desire.
ex.t: 她了解了欲望的危害。

ex.s: The activities Alice joined in helped her to become more ________.
ex.t: Alice参与的活动帮助她变得更加________。

ex.s: “What would the world be if there were no hunger?” It’s a question that Professor Crystal would ask her students.
ex.t: "如果没有饥饿，世界会是什么样？"这是Crystal教授会问她学生的问题。

ex.s: The result—an approach known as systems thinking—is now seen as essential in meeting global challenges.
ex.t: 其结果——一种被称为系统思维的方法——现在被认为对于应对全球挑战至关重要。

ex.s: According to systems thinking, changing the food system—or any other network—requires three things to happen.
ex.t: 根据系统思维，改变食物系统——或任何其他网络——需要三件事情发生。

ex.s: First, researchers need to identify all the players in that system; second, they must work out how they relate to each other; and third, they need to understand and quantify the impact of those relationships on each other and on those outside the system.
ex.t: 首先，研究人员需要识别该系统中的所有参与者；其次，他们必须弄清楚彼此之间的关系；第三，他们需要理解和量化这些关系对彼此以及对系统外各方的影响。

ex.s: Tracking of 150 biochemicals in food has been important in revealing the relationships between calories, sugar, fat and the occurrence of common diseases.
ex.t: 对食物中150种生化物质的追踪在揭示卡路里、糖、脂肪与常见疾病发生之间的关系方面发挥了重要作用。

ex.s: But using machine learning and artificial intelligence, some scientists propose that human diets consist of at least 26,000 biochemicals—and that the vast majority are not known.This shows that we have some way to travel before achieving the first objective of systems t hinking - which,in this example, is to identify more constituent parts of the nutrition system.
ex.t: 但利用机器学习和人工智能，一些科学家提出人类饮食至少包含26000种生化物质——其中绝大多数尚未被发现。这表明我们在实现系统思维的第一个目标方面还有很长的路要走——在本例中，这个目标是识别营养系统的更多组成部分。

ex.s: A systems approach to creating change is also built on the assumption that everyone in the system has equal power.
ex.t: 创建变化的系统方法还建立在这样的假设之上：系统中的每个人都拥有同等的权力。

ex.s: But as some researchers find, the food system is not an equal one.
ex.t: 但正如一些研究人员发现的，食物系统并不是一个平等的体系。

ex.s: More researchers, policymakers and representatives from the food industry must learn to look beyond their direct lines of responsibility and adopt a systems approach.
ex.t: 更多研究人员、政策制定者和食品行业代表必须学会超越其直接责任范围，采用系统思维的方法。

ex.s: The author uses the question underlined in Paragraph 1 to ________.
ex.t: 作者在第1段中使用带下划线的问题是为了________。

ex.s: introduce the topicD. predict the ending
ex.t: 引入话题D. 预测结尾

ex.s: What can be inferred about the field of nutrition?
ex.t: 关于营养领域可以推断出什么？

ex.s: The first objective of systems thinking hasn’t been achieved.
ex.t: 系统思维的第一个目标尚未实现。

ex.s: B The relationships among players have been clarified.
ex.t: B 参与者之间的关系已经明确。

ex.s: Machine learning can solve the nutrition problem.
ex.t: 机器学习可以解决营养问题。

ex.s: The impact of nutrition cannot be quantified.
ex.t: 营养的影响无法量化。

ex.s: As for systems thinking, which would the author agree with?
ex.t: 关于系统思维，作者会同意哪种说法？

ex.s: A friend has been sending me articles on how quantum computers might help solve some of the biggest challenges we face as humans.
ex.t: 一位朋友一直在给我发文章，介绍量子计算机可能如何帮助我们解决作为人类面临的一些最大挑战。

ex.s: One is computer scientist Chris Johnson who I see as someone who helps keep the field honest The other is physicist Philip Taylor.
ex.t: 一位是计算机科学家Chris Johnson，我认为他是一个有助于保持该领域诚实的人。另一位是物理学家Philip Taylor。

ex.s: As quantum computing attracts more attention and funding, researchers may mislead investors, journalists, the public and, worst of all, themselves about their work’s potential.
ex.t: 随着量子计算吸引更多关注和资金，研究人员可能会误导投资者、记者、公众，最糟糕的是误导他们自己关于其工作潜力的问题。

ex.s: After I read the book, Taylor patiently answered my questions about it.
ex.t: 读完这本书后，Taylor耐心地回答了我关于它的问题。

ex.s: He also answered my questions about PyQuantum, the firm he co-founded in 2016.
ex.t: 他还回答了我关于PyQuantum的问题，那是他在2016年联合创立的公司。

ex.s: Could PyQuantum really be leading all the competition “by a wide margin”, as Taylor claims?
ex.t: PyQuantum真的可能在竞争中"大幅领先"，正如Taylor所说的那样吗？

ex.s: Regarding Johnson’s concerns, the author feels ________.
ex.t: 关于Johnson的担忧，作者感到________。

ex.s: The competition in the field.
ex.t: 该领域的竞争。

ex.s: The investment of tech companies.
ex.t: 科技公司的投资。

ex.s: What does the underlined word “prone” in Paragraph 3 most probably mean?
ex.t: 第3段中带下划线的单词"prone"最可能是什么意思？

ex.s: The researchers believe that the findings could help technology companies develop better machines that use air to do their jobs, as suction has long been used in robotics to grab objects.

ex.s: The researchers are so impressed that they suggest the elephant’s suction technique could help improve robotics technology.

ex.s: Some scientists insist that once we discover the truth about the world, we are done.
ex.t: 一些科学家坚持认为，一旦我们发现世界的真相，任务就完成了。

ex.s: The history of science offers many examples of matters that scientists thought they had resolved, only to discover that these matters needed to be reconsidered.
ex.t: 科学史提供了许多这样的例子：科学家们以为已经解决了的问题，后来却发现需要重新考虑。

ex.s: Familiar examples include Earth as the center of the universe and the stability of continents.
ex.t: 熟悉的例子包括地球是宇宙中心以及大陆稳定不变的观点。

ex.s: The concept of beauty today is very different from what it was in ancient Greece or the Middle Ages, and so are most of our “laws” of nature.
ex.t: 如今美的概念与古希腊或中世纪时的概念大不相同，我们大多数自然"定律"也是如此。

ex.s: Other scientists may say scientific findings are true because they use “the scientific method.” But we can never actually agree on what that method is.
ex.t: 其他科学家可能会说科学发现之所以是真的，是因为它们使用了"科学方法"。但我们实际上无法就这种方法究竟是什么达成一致。

ex.s: Some will say it is observation and description of the world.
ex.t: 有人说它是对世界的观察和描述。

ex.s: Others will say it is the use of experience and experiment.
ex.t: 也有人说它是经验和实验的运用。

ex.s: Recently a leading scientist said the scientific method was to avoid fooling oneself into thinking something is true that is not.
ex.t: 最近一位顶尖科学家说，科学方法是避免自欺欺人地相信不真实的事情。

ex.s: Each of these views has its value, but if the claim is that any one of these is the scientific method, then they all fail.
ex.t: 这些观点各有价值，但如果声称其中任何一个是唯一的科学方法，那么它们都不成立。

ex.s: In fact, the methods of science have varied between disciplines and across time.
ex.t: 事实上，科学方法在不同学科之间和不同时期都有所变化。

ex.s: Scientists have bitterly argued about which methods are the best, and, as we all know, bitter arguments rarely get resolved.
ex.t: 科学家们曾激烈争论哪种方法最好，而我们都知道，激烈的争论很少能得到解决。

ex.s: In my view, science is not simple, and neither is the natural world.
ex.t: 在我看来，科学并不简单，自然界也不简单。

ex.s: Our efforts to understand and explain the natural world are just that: efforts.
ex.t: 我们理解和解释自然界的努力仅仅是努力而已。

ex.s: The good news is that when that happens, we pick ourselves up, brush ourselves off, and get back to work.
ex.t: 好消息是，当失败发生时，我们会重新站起来，拍掉身上的灰尘，继续工作。

ex.s: Understanding the world we live in, and using that knowledge to do useful things, is its own reward.
ex.t: 理解我们所生活的世界，并用这些知识做有用的事，本身就是一种回报。

ex.t: 他的工作是坐在钢琴家旁边翻乐谱，这样音乐家就不必自己翻谱而打断音乐的流畅性。

ex.s: You have to make sure you don’t turn two pages at once and make sure you find the repeats in the music when you have to go back to the right spot.” Mr Titterton explained.

ex.s: The researchers examined various levels of noise on participants as they completed tests of creative thinking.
ex.t: 由于效果很小，这可能表明我们的创造性思维在完全静默和85分贝背景噪音下的反应差别不大。

ex.s: The differences between most of the groups were statistically insignificant; however,the participants in the 70 decibels group—those exposed to a level of noise similar to background chatter in a coffee shop-significantly outperformed the other groups.
ex.t: 但由于70分贝的结果显著，这项研究也表明适当水平的背景噪音——不太响也不完全安静——实际上可能提高一个人的创造性思维能力。

ex.s: Since the effects were small, this may suggest that our creative thinking does not differ that much in response to total silence and 85 decibels of background noise.
ex.t: 适当水平的背景噪音可能刚好足以打断我们的正常思维模式而不妨碍专注，从而让我们的想象力自由驰骋。

ex.s: But since the results at 70 decibels were significant, the study also suggests that the right level of background noise—not too loud and not total silence—may actually improve one’s creative thinking ability.
ex.t: 这种"分心式的专注"似乎是从事创造性工作的最佳状态。

ex.s: This kind of "distracted focus" appears to be the best state for working on creative tasks.

ex.s: Indeed, the researchers found that face-to-face interactions and conversations affect the creative process, and yet a coworking space or a coffee shop provides a certain level of noise while also providing freedom from interruptions.

ex.s: If you ever get the impression that your dog can "tell" whether you look content or annoyed, you may be onto something.

ex.s: During the training stage, each dog was shown only the upper half or the lower half of the person’s face.
ex.t: 研究人员发现狗能够通过用鼻子触摸图片来选择生气或开心的脸而且频率高于随机概率。

ex.s: The researchers then tested the dogs’ ability to distinguish between human facial expressions by showing them the other half of the person’s face or images totally different from the ones used in training.
ex.t: 研究表明动物已经弄清楚如何在测试阶段将在训练中学到的关于人类面部的知识应用到新面孔上。

ex.s: The researchers found that the dogs were able to pick the angry or happy face by touching a picture of it with their noses more often than one would expect by random chance.
ex.t: "我们可以排除狗只是根据简单线索如牙齿的外观来区分图片的可能性，"研究作者科辛·穆勒说。

ex.s: The study showed the animals had figured out how to apply what they learned about human faces during training to new faces in the testing stage.
ex.t: "相反我们的结果表明成功的狗意识到微笑的嘴意味着和微笑的眼睛相同的事情同样的规则适用于生气的嘴意味着和生气的眼睛相同的事情。"

ex.s: "We can rule out that the dogs simply distinguish between the pictures based on a simple cue, such as the sight of teeth," said study author Corsin Muller.
ex.t: "通过我们的研究我们认为我们现在可以有信心地得出结论至少一些狗能够识别人类面部表情，"穆勒告诉Live Science。

ex.s: "Instead, our results suggest that the successful dogs realized that a smiling mouth means the same thing as smiling eyes, and the same rule applies to an angry mouth having the same meaning as angry eyes.”
ex.t: 此时还不清楚狗为什么似乎具备识别人类不同面部表情的能力。

ex.s: At this point, it is not clear why dogs seem to be equipped with the ability to recognize different facial expressions in humans.
ex.t: 这项新研究的重点是狗能否_________。

ex.s: "To us, the most likely explanation appears to be that the basis lies in their living with humans, which gives them a lot of exposure to human facial expressions," and this exposure has provided them with many chances to learn to distinguish between them, Muller said.

ex.s: The most rewarding day for our group was project day，when all the efforts we put into collecting the items finally came together．When I saw the various supplies we had collected，it hit me that every kit we were to build that day would eventually be in the hands of an Iraqi child．Over the past four months，I had never imagined how I would feel once our project was completed．While making the kits，I realized that I had lost sight of the true meaning behind it．I had only focused on the fact that it was another school project and one I wanted to get a good grade on．When the kits were completed，and ready to be sent overseas，the warm feeling I had was one I would never forget．
ex.t: 对我们小组来说最有收获的一天是项目日那天我们收集物品的所有努力终于汇聚在一起．当我看到我们收集的各种物资时我突然意识到我们当天要制作的每一个包裹最终都会送到一个伊拉克孩子手中．在过去四个月里我从没想过项目完成后我会是什么感觉．在制作包裹的过程中我意识到我已经忘记了它背后的真正意义．我只把它当作又一个学校项目而且我想在这个项目上取得好成绩．当包裹完成准备运往海外时那种温暖的感觉是我永远不会忘记的．

ex.s: In the beginning，I dared myself to make a difference in the life of another person．Now that our project is over，I realize that I have affected not only one life，but ten．With our efforts，ten young boys and girls will now be able to further their education．
ex.t: 一开始我鼓起勇气想要改变另一个人的生活．现在我们的项目结束了我意识到我影响的不只是一个生命而是十个．通过我们的努力十个伊拉克儿童现在将能够继续接受教育．
