ex.s: Hundreds of scientists, writers and academics sounded a warning to humanity in an open letter published last December: Policymakers and the rest of us must engage openly with the risk of global collapse.
ex.t: 数百名科学家、作家和学者去年12月在发表的一封公开信中向人类发出警告：政策制定者和我们所有人都必须公开面对全球崩溃的风险。

ex.s: The call for public engagement with the unthinkable is especially germane in this moment of still-uncontrolled pandemic and economic crises in the world's most technologically advanced nations.
ex.t: 公众参与讨论不可想象之事的呼吁在当今世界最发达的国家仍处于失控的大流行病和经济危机这一时刻尤其相关。

ex.s: The international scholars’ warning letter doesn't say exactly what collapse will look like or when it might happen.
ex.t: 国际学者们的警告信并没有确切说明崩溃会是什么样子或何时可能发生。

ex.s: Collapseology, the study of collapse, is more concerned with identifying trends and with them the dangers of everyday civilization.
ex.t: 崩溃学即对崩溃的研究更关注识别趋势以及与之相关的日常文明危险。

ex.s: With the current footprint of humanity, “it seems that global collapse is certain to happen in some form, possibly within a decade, certainly within this century,” Johnson said in an email.
ex.t: 以目前人类的足迹来看"全球崩溃似乎必然会发生某种形式可能在未来十年内肯定在本世纪内，"约翰逊在一封电子邮件中说。

ex.s: “Only if we discuss the consequences of our biophysical limits” the December warning letter says, “can we have the hope to reduce their speed, severity and harm”.
ex.t: "只有当我们讨论我们生物物理极限的后果时"12月的警告信说"我们才有希望降低其速度、严重性和危害"。

ex.s: And yet messengers of the coming disturbance are likely to be ignored.
ex.t: 然而即将到来的动荡的信使很可能被忽视。

ex.s: In the incurable form of hope.
ex.t: 以一种无可救药的希望形式。

ex.s: “Let's look directly into the issue of collapse,” they say, “and deal with the terrible possibilities of what we see there to make the best of a troubling future.”
ex.t: "让我们直接面对崩溃问题，"他们说，"并处理我们所看到的可怕可能性以便在令人担忧的未来中尽力而为。"

ex.s: Recently，I conceptualized a new approach to timekeeping that's connected to circumstances on our planet，conditions that might change as a result of global warming．We're now building a clock at the Anchorage Museum that reflects the total flow of several major Alaskan rivers，which are sensitive to local and global environmental changes．We've programmed it to match an atomic clock if the waterways continue to flow at their present rate．If the rivers run faster in the future on average，the clock will get ahead of standard time．If they run slower，you'll see the opposite effect．
ex.t: 最近我构想了一种与地球环境状况相关联的新型计时方式这些状况可能因全球变暖而发生变化．我们正在安克雷奇博物馆建造一座钟它反映了几条主要阿拉斯加河流的总流量这些河流对当地和全球的环境变化都很敏感．我们已经编程让它在水流保持当前速率时与原子钟同步．如果将来河流平均流速加快钟会比标准时间走得快．如果河流变慢你会看到相反的效果．

ex.s: Even if this method of timekeeping is novel in its particulars，early agricultural societies also connected time to natural phenomena．In pre-Classical Greece，for instance，people“corrected”official calendars by shifting dates forward or backward to reflect the change of season．Temporal connection to the environment was vital to their survival．Likewise，river time and other timekeeping systems we're developing may encourage environmental awareness．
ex.t: 即使这种计时方法的具体细节是新颖的早期农业社会也将时间与自然现象联系起来．例如在前古典希腊时期人们通过向前或向后调整日期来"修正"官方历法以反映季节的变化．与环境的时间联系对他们的生存至关重要．同样河流时间和其他我们正在开发的计时系统可能会促进环保意识．

ex.s: Recent research suggests that if an argument gets resolved，the emotional response tied to it is significantly reduced or almost completely erased．Thus，it may be worth bringing up issues with your friends， family members，or classmates rather than holding them back．
ex.t: 最近的研究表明如果一场争论得到解决与之相关的情绪反应会显著减少或几乎完全消除。因此与其压抑不如和朋友、家 人或同学把问题提出来可能最终会有更好的结果。

ex.s: Moreover，the older you are，the more likely you will come to a resolution after an argument．This may be because more life experience usually leads to more defined priorities．You are more likely to distinguish between what matters and what does not．
ex.t: 此外年龄越大争论后达成解决方案的可能性越大这可能是因为更多的人生经历通常会导致更明确的优先级你更有可能区分什么是重要的什么是不重要的。

ex.s: Jennifer Mauer has needed more willpower than the typical college student to pursue her goal of earning a nursing degree.
ex.t: 珍妮弗·莫尔在追求护理学位的目标上比典型的大学生需要更多的意志力。

ex.s: That willpower bore fruit when Jennifer graduated from University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire and became the first in her large family to earn a bachelor’s degree.
ex.t: 这种意志力在她从威斯康星大学欧克莱尔分校毕业并成为她大家庭中第一个获得学士学位的人时结出了果实。

ex.s: Her dad worked at a job away from the farm, and her mother ran the farm with the kids.
ex.t: 她父亲在外工作母亲带着孩子们经营农场。

ex.s: She chose the UW-Eau Claire program at Ministry Saint Joseph’s Hospital in Marshfield because she was able to pursue her four-year degree close to home.

ex.s: In the mid-1990s, Tom Bissell taught English as a volunteer in Uzbekistan.
ex.t: 在20世纪90年代中期汤姆·比塞尔作为志愿者在乌兹别克斯坦教英语。

ex.s: A few years later, still attracted to the country, he returned to Uzbekistan to write an article about the disappearance of the Aral Sea.
ex.t: 几年后仍然被这个国家吸引他回到乌兹别克斯坦写一篇关于咸海消失的文章。

ex.s: Hence this book, Chasing the Sea: Lost Among the Ghosts of Empire in Central Asia, which talks about a road trip from Tashkent to Karakalpakstan, where millions of lives have been destroyed by the slow drying up of the sea.
ex.t: 于是就有了这本书《追逐大海：在中亚帝国幽灵中迷失》书中讲述了从塔什干到卡拉卡尔帕克斯坦的公路旅行在那里数百万人的生活因咸海缓慢干涸而被摧毁。

ex.s: It is the story of an American travelling to a strange land, and of the people he meets on his way: Rustam, his translator, a lovely 24-year-old who picked up his colorful English in California, Oleg and Natasha, his hosts in Tashkent, and a string of foreign aid workers.
ex.t: 这是一个美国人前往陌生土地的故事以及他在路上遇到的人们：拉斯塔姆他的翻译一位可爱的24岁年轻人在加利福尼亚学会了地道的英语奥列格和娜塔莎他在塔什干的东道主以及一系列外国援助工作者。

ex.s: In Samarkand, Mr Bissell admires the architectural wonders, while on his way to Bukhara he gets a taste of police methods when suspected of drug dealing.

ex.s: The longest track and field event at the Summer Olympics is the 50-kilometer race walk, which is about five miles longer than the marathon.

ex.s: However, race walking does not pound the body as much as running does, Dr Norberg says.
ex.t: 根据她的研究，跑步者每步着地时承受的重量可达体重的4倍，而不离地的竞走者每步只产生约1.4倍体重的压力。

ex.s: According to her research, runners hit the ground with as much as four times their body weight per step, while race walkers, who do not leave the ground, create only about 1.4 times their body weight with each step.
ex.t: 因此，她说，跑步相关的一些伤害如跑步膝等在竞走运动员中并不常见。

ex.s: As a result, she says, some of the injuries associated with running, such as runner’s knee, are uncommon among race walkers.
ex.t: 但这项运动的奇特形式确实会给脚踝和髋部带来相当大的压力，所以有过此类伤病史的人在选择这项运动时应谨慎。

ex.t: 事实上，任何想尝试竞走的人最好先请教教练或有经验的竞走者学习正确的技巧，她说。

ex.s: The connection between people and plants has long been the subject of scientific research.

ex.s: The engineers at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology（MIT）have taken it a step further changing the actual composition of plants in order to get them to perform diverse，even unusual functions.
ex.t: 这些包括叶片上印有传感器以显示何时缺水的植物，以及能够检测地下水中有害化学物质的植物。"我们在思考如何改造植物来替代我们每天使用的物品的功能，"MIT化学工程教授Michael Strano解释道。

ex.s: These include plants that have sensors printed onto their leaves to show when they’re short of water and a plant that can detect harmful chemicals in groundwater. ＂We’re thinking about how we can engineer plants to replace functions of the things that we use every day,＂explained Michael Strano, a professor of chemical engineering at MIT.
ex.t: Strano的团队发现他们可以发出微弱的光，持续三个半小时。

ex.s: The technology, Strano said, could one day be used to light the rooms or even to turn tree into self-powered street lamps.

ex.s: The researchers analyzed video recordings of 53 child-parent pairs during everyday activities at home and found children who play with puzzles between 26 and 46 months of age have better spatial skills when assessed at 54 months of age.

ex.s: My first job was working at the Ukiah Library when I was 16 years old .It was a dream job and I did everything from shelving books to reading to the children for story time.
ex.t: 我的第一份工作是16岁时在Ukiah图书馆工作。这是一份梦想般的工作，我从上架图书到给孩子们读书讲故事什么都做。

ex.s: As I grew older and became a mother, the library took on a new place and an added meaning in my life.
ex.t: 随着我长大并成为母亲，图书馆在我的生活中有了新的位置和额外的意义。

ex.s: It was a big deal for us to load up and go to the local library, where my kids could pick out books to read or books they wanted me to read to them.
ex.t: 对我们来说，装车去当地图书馆是一件大事，在那里我的孩子们可以选择自己读的书或者想让我读给他们听的书。

ex.s: I always read ,using different voices ,as though I were acting out the stories with my voice and they loved it !It was a special time to bond with my children and it filled them with the wonderment of books .
ex.t: 我总是用不同的声音朗读，就像我在用声音表演故事一样，他们很喜欢！那是与孩子们建立联系的特别时光，充满了书籍带来的奇妙感觉。

ex.s: Now, I see my children taking their children to the library and I love that the excitement of going to the library lives on form generation to generation.
ex.t: 现在，我看到我的孩子们带着他们的孩子去图书馆，我很高兴去图书馆的兴奋之情一代代传承下去。

ex.s: Yet "Apes" is more exception than the rule.

ex.s: Already, a number of films, including "Water for Elephants," "The Hangover Part Ⅱ" and "Zookeeper," have drawn the anger of activists who say the creatures acting in them haven’t been treated properly.

ex.s: In some cases, it’s not so much the treatment of the animals on set in the studio that has activists worried; it’s the off-set training and living conditions that are raising concerns.

ex.t: 然而，当我思考Juan的问题时，我不确定我们还能排除多少可能性。

ex.t: 我们知道什么和不知道什么的问题一直困扰着我。

ex.s: The number of trees larger than two feet across has declined by 50 percent on more than 46, 000 square miles of California forests, the new study finds.
ex.t: 一项新研究发现，在加利福尼亚州超过46,000平方英里的森林中，直径超过两英尺的大树数量已经减少了50%。

ex.s: No area was spared or unaffected, from the foggy northern coast to the Sierra Nevada Mountains to the San Gabriels above Los Angeles.
ex.t: 从雾蒙蒙的北海岸到内华达山脉到洛杉矶上方的圣盖博山，没有哪个地区幸免或未受影响。

ex.s: In the Sierra high country, the number of big trees has fallen by more than 55 percent; in parts of southern California the decline was nearly 75 percent.
ex.t: 在内华达高海拔地区，大树的数量下降了超过55%；在南加州部分地区，下降幅度接近75%。

ex.s: Many factors contributed to the decline, said Patrick Mclntyre, an ecologist who was the lead author of the study.
ex.t: 多种因素导致了这种下降，该研究的主要作者、生态学家帕特里克·麦金太尔说。

ex.s: Housing development pushed into the woods.
ex.t: 住房开发向森林推进。

ex.s: But in comparing a study of California forests done in the 1920s and 1930s with another one between 2001 and 2010, Mclntyre and his colleagues documented a widespread death of big trees that was evident even in wildlands protected from woodcutting or development.
ex.t: 但麦金太尔和他的同事在比较20世纪20年代和30年代的加州森林研究与2001年至2010年之间的另一项研究时发现，即使在没有伐木或开发保护的荒野地区，大树的广泛死亡也是显而易见的。

ex.s: The loss of big trees was greatest in areas where trees had suffered the greatest water shortage.
ex.t: 大树的损失在树木遭受最严重缺水的地区最为严重。

ex.s: Since the 1930s, Mclntyre said, the biggest factors driving up water stress in the state have been rising temperatures, which cause trees to lose more water to the air, and earlier snowmelt, which reduces the water supply available to trees during the dry season.
ex.t: 麦金太尔说，自20世纪30年代以来，导致该州水压力上升的最大因素是气温上升——气温上升导致树木向空气中散失更多水分——以及融雪提前——融雪提前减少了旱季树木可用的供水量。

By giving kids a lot of praise, parents think they're building their children's confidence, when, in fact, it may be just the opposite.
ex.t: 世界各地的父母都在夸奖他们的孩子。

ex.s: Still, don't go too far in the other direction.
ex.t: 过度的赞扬可能会适得其反，而且当以不真诚的方式给予时，会使孩子害怕尝试新事物或冒险，因为他们担心无法保持在父母赞扬把他们所放置的位置上。

ex.s: Experts say that the quality of praise is more important than the quantity.
ex.t: 那么多少赞扬才是适当的呢？

ex.s: If praise is sincere and focused on the effort not the outcome, you can give it as often as your child does something that deserves a verbal reward." We should especially recognize our children's efforts to push themselves and work hard to achieve a goal, "says Donahue, author of Parenting Without Fear: Letting Go of Worry and Focusing on What Really Matters.
ex.t: 专家说赞扬的质量比数量更重要。

ex.s: "One thing to remember is that it's the process not the end product that matters."

ex.s: I must have always known reading was very important because the first memories I have as a child deal with books． There was not one night that I don't remember mom reading me a storybook by my bedside． I was extremely inspired by the elegant way the words sounded．
ex.t: （5）教师委员会在2月19日将要做什么？

ex.s: I always wanted to know what my mom was reading． Hearing mom say，"I can't believe what's printed in the newspaper this morning，" made me want to grab it out of her hands and read it myself． I wanted to be like my mom and know all of the things she knew． So I carried around a book， and each night， just to be like her， I would pretend to be reading．
ex.t: A．预览表演和纪录片。

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．
ex.t: B．对材料发表评论。

ex.s: Yet， now that I'm growing and the world I once knew as being so simple is becoming more complex， I find myself needing a way to escape． By opening a novel， I can leave behind my burdens and enter into a wonderful and mysterious world where I am now a new character． In these worlds I can become anyone． I don't have to write down what happened or what technique the author was using when he or she wrote this． I just read to relax．

ex.s: We're taught to read because it's necessary for much of human understanding． Reading is a vital part of my life． Reading satisfies my desire to keep learning． And I've found that the possibilities that lie within books are limitless．

ex.s: So while some of the world's first coins were made from a naturally occurring hybrid of gold and silver called electrum, objects other than coins have served as currency, including beads, ivory, livestock, and cowrie shells.
ex.t: 在整个殖民时期，烟草在弗吉尼亚州、马里兰州和北卡罗来纳州被用来代替硬币或纸币，尽管它在殖民地其他地方以及整个欧洲和英国也被广泛使用

ex.s: In West Africa, bracelets of bronze or copper were used as cash, especially if the transaction was associated with the slave trade there.
ex.t: 今天，在太平洋的一个岛屿上，一种特定类型的贝壳仍然作为货币——有些人甚至囤积它，就像比特币大亨一样，坚信有一天它会让他们变得富得无法想象。

ex.s: Throughout the colonial period, tobacco was used in lieu of coins or paper bills in Virginia, Maryland and North Carolina, even though it was used elsewhere in the colonies and extensively throughout Europe and the UK
ex.t: 在马莱塔——所罗门群岛人口最多的岛屿——贝壳在大多数地方都被接受，"你的贝壳能换多少金枪鱼取决于它们的颜色和形状，"来自马莱塔小镇奥基的店主玛丽·布鲁诺告诉Vice杂志。

ex.s: Today, on an island in the Pacific, a specific type of shell still serves as currency — and some people there are even hoarding it, just like Bitcoin moguls, convinced that one day, it will make them wealthy beyond imagination.
ex.t: "一条深色贝壳可能换到两罐小金枪鱼，但红色的价值更高，对于红色贝壳，一条可能换到足够养活一个大家庭很长时间的金枪鱼。

ex.s: On Malaita, the most- populated island that’s part of the Solomon Islands, shells are accepted at most places in “How much tuna you can get for your shells depends on their color and shape,” Mary Bruno, a shop owner from the small town of Auki, on Malaita, told Vice.
ex.t: 就像铸造硬币一样，岛上只有一个地方制作这些贝壳——它们被打磨后串成3英尺长的绳子。

ex.s: Just like a mint that creates coins, there' s only one place on the island where the shells, which are polished and strung together to form 3-foot-long ropes, are made.
ex.t: 一旦被困在他们的岛上，当地人需要一种在他们之间使用的货币，于是贝壳货币诞生了。

ex.s: (You can see how that works in the video above.) The strips of red, white, and black shells all come from Langa Langa Lagoon, where artificial islands were long-ago built by locals to escape from the island-dwelling cannibals.
ex.t: 使用贝壳作为货币在整个太平洋岛屿直到20世纪初仍很普遍，但马莱塔的独特之处在于它们至今仍在使用。

ex.s: Once marooned out on their islands, locals needed a currency to use among themselves, and so the shell currency was born.
ex.t: 就像加密货币一样，也有人认为岛民投资这种货币是明智的，据报道这种货币的价值在过去三十年中有所上升。

ex.s: Using shells for money was common throughout the Pacific islands as late as the early 1900s, but Malaita is unique in that they are still used today.
ex.t: 囤积一堆加工过的、串在一起的贝壳似乎很奇怪，但一堆美元又算什么呢？

ex.s: And just like crypto currencies, there are those who think the islanders are smart to invest in this type of money, which is reported to have risen in value over the last three decades.
ex.t: 只是一张专门印刷的纸和大麻纤维，我们赋予了它价值——而且随着时间的推移可能比那些贝壳更不耐用。

ex.t: 今年早些时候，爱达荷州博伊西市的居民惴惴不安地看着这棵城市最古老最高的居民移动了两个街区。

ex.s: Inhabitants of Boise, Idaho, watched with trepidation earlier this year as the city's oldest, tallest resident moved two blocks.
ex.t: 这家总部位于德克萨斯的公司开发并获得专利了一种挖掘和搬运技术来移动巨大的树木。

ex.s: The 105-year-old sequoia tree serves as a local landmark, not only for its longevity but also because renowned naturalist and Sierra Club cofounder John Muir provided the original seedling.
ex.t: 这棵博伊西巨杉重超过80万磅，是他们迄今为止最大的工程。

ex.s: The Texas-based company has developed and patented scooping and lifting technology to move massive trees.
ex.t: "我[已经]为此失去了足够的睡眠，"该公司西部副总裁大卫·考克斯说——那还是在医院提到这棵树的显赫出身之前。

ex.s: Weighing in at more than 800, 000 pounds, the Boise sequoia is its largest undertaking yet.
ex.t: 在重型搬运开始之前，团队评估了根系并在树干周围挖了一个五英尺深、直径40英尺的圆柱体来保护所有重要的根。

ex.s: Before the heavy lifting began, the team assessed the root system and dug a five-foot-deep cylinder , measuring 40 feet in diameter, around the trunk to protect all essential roots.
ex.t: 插图详细描述了随后发生的事情。——莱斯利·内莫

ex.s: After encapsulating the root ball in wire mesh, the movers allowed the tree to acclimate to its new situation for seven months before relocating it.
ex.t: 默里特和他的环境设计团队在根球下方安装了一个由7英寸直径、44英尺长的钢棒组成的平台，就在钢棒下方安装了一组未充气的气囊（灰色显示）。团队还挖了一个浅坡道。

ex.s: The illustration details what followed. — Leslie Nemo
ex.t: 大约15分钟后，搬运人员将气囊充气至约三英尺直径，将根球提升到洞口表面。

ex.s: Merit and his team at Environmental Design installed underneath the root ball a platform of seven-inch-diameter,44-foot-long steelbars and, just below the rods, a first set of uninflated airbags ( shown in gray).The team also dug a shallow ramp.
ex.t: 通过对前方的气囊充气不足，团队让承载树木的平台沿坡道滚出洞口同时保持水平，一辆拖车拉着树木前行，同时团队成员从平台后面取下气囊并在前面重新安装。

ex.s: In roughly 15 minutes, the movers inflated the airbags to about three feet in diameter to raise the root ball to the surface of the hole.
ex.t: 他们重复这个过程直到树木到达它新家的边缘。

ex.s: By underinflating the front bags, the team allowed the platform carrying the tree to roll up the ramp and out of the hole while staying level, A trailer hauled the tree along as team members removed the airbags from the back of the platform and replaced them in the front.
ex.t: 那里有一组部分充气的气囊（白色显示）在洞内等候。

ex.s: They repeated the process until the tree arrived at the edge of its new home.
ex.t: 巨杉原来位置周围的土壤也被迁移了，因为树木带着原来的土壤移植时更容易存活。

ex.s: There a second set of partially inflated bags (shown in white) waited inside the hole.
ex.t: 使用第一组气囊，搬运人员将平台滚入新坑。

ex.s: Soil surrounding the sequoia in its original location was relocated as well, because trees are more likely to survive a transplant when they move with their original soil.
ex.t: 等候在那里的气囊然后进一步充气以承受巨杉的重量，同时运输气囊被放气并从树下移走。

ex.s: Using the first set of airbags, the movers rolled the platform into the new hole.
ex.t: 白色气囊然后在约半小时内放气以将巨杉的根球降到坑底，气囊被移走了，但钢棒留在了树上因为它们会在数年内生锈降解。

ex.s: The bags waiting there were then inflated further to take the weight of the sequoia while the transportation bags were deflated and removed from under the tree.
ex.t: 在接下来的五年里，当地公园服务部门将在巨杉的新家对其进行监测和维护。

ex.s: The white bags were then deflated in about half an hour to lower the sequoia's root ball to the bottom of its hole, The bags were removed, but the metal bars were left with the tree because they rust and degrade over a number of years.
ex.t: 以下哪个词可以替换划线的"stood in the way of"？

ex.s: For the next five years the local park service will monitor and maintain the tree in its new home.
ex.t: 巨杉树搬迁的原因是什么？

ex.s: Which of the following words can be used to replace the words underlined "stood in the way of"?
ex.t: 因为挖掘和搬运技术应该投入使用。

ex.s: What is the reason for the relocation of Sequoia trees?
ex.t: 因为它阻碍了当地医院的扩建计划。

ex.s: Because the Scooping and lifting technology should be put into use.
ex.t: 因为它符合政府的环境设计计划。

ex.s: How will the migrated sequoia trees be dealt with?
ex.t: 用于移动巨杉树的金属杆不会留在树上。

ex.s: They will be given new soil in the new living environment.
ex.t: 它们将一直在运输袋中保存。

ex.s: Metal rods used to move sequoia trees will not be left on the trees.
ex.t: 它们将在未来五年由专家管理。

ex.s: They will be kept in transport bags all the time.
ex.t: 理解预算线的经济概念

ex.s: They will be managed by specialists in the next five years.
ex.t: "预算线"一词有几个相关含义，包括几个显而易见的含义和一个不太明显的含义。

ex.s: Understand the Economic Concept of a Budget Line
ex.t: 作为非正式消费者理解的预算线

ex.s: The term “budget line” has several related meanings, including a couple that are self- evident and a third that is not.
ex.t: 预算线是一个大多数消费者无需图表和方程就能直观理解的基本概念——例如家庭预算。

ex.s: The budget line as an Informal Consumer Understanding
ex.t: 非正式地说，预算线描述了给定预算和特定商品的可承受能力边界。

ex.s: The budget line is an elementary concept that most consumers understand intuitively without a need for graphs and equations — it's the household budget, for example.
ex.t: 给定有限金额的钱，消费者只能花费相同金额购买商品。

ex.s: Taken informally, the budget line describes the boundary of affordability for a given budget and specific goods.
ex.t: 如果消费者有X金额的钱并且想购买两种商品A和B，她只能购买总计X的商品。

ex.s: If the consumer has X amount of money and wants to buy two goods A and B, she can only purchase goods totaling X.
ex.t: 这似乎太显而易见了以至于不值得写下来或阅读。

ex.s: If the consumer needs an amount of A costing 0.75, she can then spend only 0.25 X, the amount remaining, on her purchase of B.
ex.t: 然而，事实证明，这个概念——大多数消费者每天都会多次做出这个决定而不需要思考——是经济学中更正式的预算线概念的基础，下文将对此进行解释。

ex.s: As it turns out, however, this same concept-one that most consumers make many times each day with reflecting on it-is the basis of the more formal budget line concept in economics , which is explained below.
ex.t: 在转到预算线的经济学定义之前，考虑另一个概念：逐项预算。

ex.s: Before turning to the economics definition of budget line, consider another concept: the line-item budget.
ex.t: 这种用法没有什么复杂的地方，预算线就是预算中的一行，上面注明了要购买的服务或商品及其成本，

ex.s: This is effectively a map of future expenditures, with all the constituent expenditures individually noted and quantified.
ex.t: 作为经济学概念的预算线

ex.s: There' s nothing very complicated about this usage, a budget line is one of the lines in the budget, with the service or good to be purchased named and the cost quantified,
ex.t: 经济学研究与人类一般行为的关系的一个有趣方式是，许多经济理论是上述简单概念的正式化——消费者对自己拥有的金额以及这笔金额能买到什么的非正式理解。

ex.s: The Budget Line as an Economics Concept
ex.t: 在形式化的过程中，这个概念可以被表达为一个可以普遍应用的数学方程。

ex.s: One of the interesting ways the study of economics relates to human behavior generally is that a lot of economic theory is the formalization of the kind of simple concept outlined above — a consumer's informal understanding of the amount she has to spend and what that amount will buy.
ex.t: 一个简单的预算线图

ex.s: In the process of formalization, the concept can be expressed as a mathematical equation that can be applied generally.
ex.t: 要理解这一点，想象一张图，其中垂直线量化你可以购买多少张电影票。水平线量化你可以购买多少本犯罪小说。

ex.s: To understand this, think of a graph where the vertical lines quantify how many movie tickets. you can buy and where the horizontal lines do the same for crime novels.
ex.t: 这两项更正式的经济学术语是预算集。

ex.s: You like going to the movies and reading crime novels and you have $ 150 to spend, In the example below, assume that each movie costs $10 and each crime novel costs $15.
ex.t: 如果电影每张10美元，那么用可用资金你能看的电影的最大数量是15部。

ex.s: The more formal economics term for these two items is budget set.
ex.t: 要记录这一点，你在图表的最左侧数字15处（总电影票数）做一个标记。

ex.s: If movies cost $ 10 each, then the maximum number of movies you can see with the money available is 15.
ex.t: 这个点也出现在水平轴最左端"0"的上方因为你没有剩余的钱买书——在这个例子中书的数量是0。

ex.s: To note this you make a dot at the number 15 (for total movie tickets) at the extreme left-hand side of the chart.
ex.t: 你也可以画出另一个极端——全是犯罪小说没有电影。

ex.s: This same dot appears at the extreme left above “0” on the horizontal axis because you have no money left for books — the number of books available in this example is 0.
ex.t: 由于例子中的犯罪小说每本15美元而你可用150美元，如果你把所有可用的钱都花在犯罪小说上，你可以买10本。

ex.s: You can also graph the other extreme — all crime novels and no movies.
ex.t: 所以你在水平轴数字10处做一个标记。

ex.s: Minutes after the last movie ended yesterday at the Plaza Theater, employees were busy sweeping up popcorns and gathering coke cups.

ex.s: It was a scene that had been repeated many times in the theater’s 75-year history.
ex.t: 这一幕在这座剧院75年的历史中重复了许多次。

ex.s: This time, however, the cleanup was a little different.
ex.t: 但这一次，清理工作有点不同。

ex.s: As one group of workers carried out the rubbish, another group began removing seats and other theater equipment in preparation for the building’s end.
ex.t: 当一组工人运走垃圾时，另一组工人开始拆除座椅和其他剧院设备，为建筑的终结做准备。

ex.s: The film classic The Last Picture Show was the last movie shown in the old theater.
ex.t: 经典影片《最后一场电影》是这座老剧院放映的最后一部电影。

ex.s: Though the movie is 30 years old, most of the 250 seats were filled with teary-eyed audience wanting to say good-bye to the old building.
ex.t: 尽管这部电影已有30年历史，但250个座位几乎坐满了眼含泪水的观众，他们想向这座老建筑告别。

ex.s: Theater owner Ed Bradford said he chose the movie because it seemed appropriate.
ex.t: 剧院老板埃德·布拉德福德说他选择这部电影是因为它似乎很合适。

ex.s: The movie is set in a small town where the only movie theater is preparing to close down.
ex.t: 电影背景设定在一个小镇，镇上唯一的电影院正准备关门。

ex.s: Bradford said that large modern theaters in the city made it impossible for the Plaza to compete.
ex.t: 布拉德福德说城里的大型现代剧院使得广场影院无法与之竞争。

ex.s: “This used to be the center of town,” he said.
ex.t: "这里曾经是镇中心，"他说。

ex.s: “Now the area is mostly office buildings and warehouses.”
ex.t: "现在这一带大多是办公楼和仓库。"

ex.s: Last week some city officials suggested the city might be interested in turning the old theater into a museum and public meeting place.
ex.t: 上周一些市政府官员表示，市里可能有兴趣把这座老剧院改建成博物馆和公共场所。

ex.s: Bradford sold the building and land to a local development firm, which plans to build a shopping complex on the land where the theater is located.
ex.t: 布拉德福德把大楼和土地卖给了一家当地开发公司，该公司计划在剧院所在地建造一个购物中心。

ex.s: The theater audience said good-bye as Bradford locked the doors for the last time.
ex.t: 当布拉德福德最后一次锁门时，剧院观众告别了。

ex.s: Fourteen wolves were caught in Canada and transported to the park.
ex.t: 在加拿大捕获了14只狼并被运送到公园。

ex.s: By last year, the Yellowstone wolf population had grown to more than 170 wolves.
ex.t: 到去年为止，黄石地区的灰狼数量已增长到170多只。

ex.s: Gray wolves once were seen here and there in the Yellowstone area and much of the continental United States, but they were gradually displaced by human development.
ex.t: 灰狼曾经出现在黄石地区和美国大陆许多地方，但由于人类活动的影响，它们逐渐被驱逐。

ex.s: By the 1920s, wolves had practically disappeared from the Yellowstone area.
ex.t: 到20世纪20年代，灰狼实际上已从黄石地区消失。

ex.s: They went farther north into the deep forests of Canada, where there were fewer humans around.
ex.t: 它们向北迁移进入加拿大深处的森林，那里人类较少。

ex.s: The disappearance of the wolves had many unexpected results.
ex.t: 灰狼的消失带来了许多意想不到的结果。

ex.s: In the absence of wolves, coyote populations also grew quickly.
ex.t: 在没有狼的情况下，郊狼的数量也迅速增长。

ex.s: The coyotes killed a large percentage of the park’s red foxes, and completely drove away the park’s beavers.
ex.t: 郊狼杀死了公园中很大比例的红狐，并将河狸完全赶出了公园。

ex.s: As early as 1966, biologists asked the government to consider reintroducing wolves to Yellowstone Park.
ex.t: 早在1966年，生物学家就请求政府考虑将狼重新引入黄石公园。

ex.s: They hoped that wolves would be able to control the elk and coyote problems.
ex.t: 他们希望狼能够控制麋鹿和郊狼的问题。

ex.s: Many farmers opposed the plan because they feared that wolves would kill their farm animals or pets.
ex.t: 许多农民反对这项计划，因为他们担心狼会杀死他们的农场动物或宠物。

ex.s: The government spent nearly 30 years coming up with a plan to reintroduce the wolvers.
ex.t: 政府花了近30年时间制定重新引入狼的计划。

ex.s: The US Fish and Wildlife Service carefully monitors and manages the wolf packs in Yellowstone.
ex.t: 美国鱼类和野生动物管理局仔细监测和管理黄石公园的狼群。

ex.s: Today, the debate continues over how well the gray wolf is fitting in at Yellowstone.
ex.t: 今天，关于灰狼在黄石的适应情况如何，争论仍在继续。

ex.s: The Yellowstone wolf project has been a valuable experiment to help biologists decide whether to reintroduce wolves to other parts of the country as well.
ex.t: 黄石狼项目是一项有价值的实验，有助于生物学家决定是否也将狼重新引入美国其他地区。

ex.s: The Intelligent Transport team at Newcastle University have turned an electric car into a mobile laboratory named “Drive LAB” in order to understand the challenges faced by older drivers and to discover where the key stress points are.
ex.t: 纽卡斯尔大学的智能交通团队将一辆电动汽车改装成了名为"Drive LAB"的移动实验室，目的是了解老年驾驶员面临的挑战并发现关键的压力点在哪里。

ex.s: Led by Professor Phil Blythe, the Newcastle team are developing in-vehicle technologies for older drivers which they hope could help them to continue driving into later life.
ex.t: 在菲尔·布莱斯教授的领导下，纽卡斯尔团队正在为老年驾驶员开发车载技术，他们希望这些技术能帮助他们在晚年继续驾驶。

ex.s: Phil Blythe explains: “For many older people, particularly those living alone or in the country, driving is important for preserving their independence, giving them the freedom to get out and about without having to rely on others.”
ex.t: 菲尔·布莱斯解释道："对许多老年人来说，特别是那些独居或在乡村生活的人来说，驾驶对于保持独立性非常重要，让他们能够自由出行而不必依赖他人。"

ex.s: The result is that people stop driving before they really need to.”
ex.t: 结果就是人们在真正需要停止驾驶之前就已经放弃了开车。"

ex.s: Dr Amy Guo, the leading researcher on the older driver study, explains, “The Drive LAB is helping us to understand what the key points and difficulties are for older drivers and how we might use technology to address these problems.
ex.t: 老年驾驶员研究的首席研究员艾米·郭博士解释说："Drive LAB帮助我们了解老年驾驶员的关键问题和困难所在，以及我们可以如何利用技术来解决这些问题。

ex.s: “For example, most of us would expect older drivers always go slower than everyone else but surprisingly, we found that in 30mph zones they struggled to keep at a constant speed and so were more likely to break the speed limit and be at risk of getting fined.
ex.t: "例如，我们大多数人可能预期老年驾驶员总是比别人慢，但令人惊讶的是，我们发现他们在30英里/小时的区域内很难保持匀速，因此更容易超速并有被罚款的风险。

ex.s: Recently，I conceptualized a new approach to timekeeping that's connected to circumstances on our planet，conditions that might change as a result of global warming．We're now building a clock at the Anchorage Museum that reflects the total flow of several major Alaskan rivers，which are sensitive to local and global environmental changes．We've programmed it to match an atomic clock if the waterways continue to flow at their present rate．If the rivers run faster in the future on average，the clock will get ahead of standard time．If they run slower，you'll see the opposite effect．
ex.t: 最近我构想了一种与地球环境状况相关联的新型计时方式这些状况可能因全球变暖而发生变化．我们正在安克雷奇博物馆建造一座钟它反映了几条主要阿拉斯加河流的总流量这些河流对当地和全球的环境变化都很敏感．我们已经编程让它在水流保持当前速率时与原子钟同步．如果将来河流平均流速加快钟会比标准时间走得快．如果河流变慢你会看到相反的效果．

ex.s: Even if this method of timekeeping is novel in its particulars，early agricultural societies also connected time to natural phenomena．In pre-Classical Greece，for instance，people“corrected”official calendars by shifting dates forward or backward to reflect the change of season．Temporal connection to the environment was vital to their survival．Likewise，river time and other timekeeping systems we're developing may encourage environmental awareness．

ex.s: A lengthy, positive review, on the other hand, was regarded as suspicious, and participants tended to trust writers that kept their glowing reviews short.

ex.s: Scientists at Salk Institute are making use of the natural capacity of plants to absorb carbon dioxide by enhancing their root systems.

ex.s: To design these climate-saving plants, the scientists are using a research tool called SLEAP — an AI software that tracks multiple features of root growth.

ex.t: SLEAP由萨尔克研究员塔尔莫·佩雷拉创建，最初设计用于在实验室中追踪动物运动。

ex.s: Now, Pereira has teamed up with plant scientist Professor Wolfgang Busch to apply SLEAP to plants.
ex.t: 现在，佩雷拉与植物学家沃尔夫冈·布施教授合作，将SLEAP应用于植物研究。

ex.s: In a study published in Plant Phenomics, Busch and Pereira establish a new procedure for using SLEAP to analyze plant root phenotypes — how deep and wide they grow, how massive their root systems become, and other physical qualities.
ex.t: 在一项发表于《植物表型组学》的研究中，布施和佩雷拉建立了使用SLEAP分析植物根系表型的新程序——包括它们生长的深度和广度、根系变得多么庞大以及其他物理特性。

ex.s: Prior to SLEAP, tracking the physical characteristics of both plants and animals required a lot of labor that slowed the scientific process.
ex.t: 在SLEAP出现之前，追踪植物和动物的物理特征需要大量人力，这减缓了科学研究进程。

ex.s: This allows the Salk team to determine what genes are most beneficial to their plant designs.

ex.s: The benefits of print reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from posing simple tasks — like identifying the main idea in a reading passage — to ones that require mental abstraction — such as drawing inferences from a text.
ex.t: 当实验者从布置简单任务（如找出阅读段落的主旨）转向需要抽象思维的任务（如从文本中推断结论）时，纸质阅读的优势就格外明显地显现出来。

ex.s: The differences between print and digital reading results are partly related to paper’s physical properties.
ex.t: 纸质阅读与电子阅读效果之间的差异，部分与纸张的物理特性有关。

ex.s: According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.
ex.t: 根据这一理论，人们以一种适合社交媒体的心态对待电子文本——往往不那么严肃，投入的脑力也比读纸质文本时少。

ex.s: However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.

ex.s: Given the astonishing potential of AI to transform our lives, we all need to take action to deal with our AI-powered future, and this is where AI by Design: A Plan for Living with Artificial Intelligence comes in.
ex.t: 鉴于人工智能改变我们生活的惊人潜力，我们都需要行动起来应对人工智能驱动的未来，这正是《设计人工智能：与人工智能共处的规划》一书的意义所在。

ex.s: As we soon come to learn from AI by Design AI is already super-smart and will become more capable, moving from the current generation of “narrow-AI” to Artificial General Intelligence.
ex.t: 正如我们很快就能从《设计人工智能》中了解到的那样，人工智能已经超级聪明，并且将变得更强大，从当前的“狭义人工智能”发展到通用人工智能。

ex.s: This is why Campbell has set out to raise awareness of AI and its future now — several decades before these developments are expected to take place.
ex.t: 这就是为什么坎贝尔现在就开始提高人们对人工智能及其未来的认识——比这些发展预计发生的时间早了几十年。

ex.s: Campbell’s point is to wake up those responsible for AI—the technology companies and world leaders—so they are on the same page as all the experts currently developing it.
ex.t: 坎贝尔的目的是唤醒那些对人工智能负责的人——科技公司和世界领导人——让他们与目前开发人工智能的所有专家达成共识。

ex.s: She explains we are at a “tipping point” in history and must act now to prevent an extinction-level event for humanity.
ex.t: 她解释说，我们正处于历史的“临界点”，必须立即行动，以防止人类遭遇灭顶之灾。

ex.s: We need to consider how we want our future with AI to pan out.
ex.t: 我们需要思考希望我们与人工智能的未来如何展开。

ex.s: Such structured thinking, followed by global regulation, will enable us to achieve greatness rather than our downfall.
ex.t: 这种有条理的思考，加上全球性的监管，将使我们成就伟大，而不是走向衰落。

ex.t: 这些社会情感让我们的大脑准备好按照家庭和社区的规范与价值观来塑造我们的行为。

ex.s: More generally, social instincts motivate us to learn how to behave in a socially complex world.
ex.t: 更广泛地说，社会本能促使我们学习如何在复杂的社会环境中行事。

ex.s: Our brains use the system to acquire behavioural patterns regarding safe routes home, efficient food gathering and dangers to avoid.
ex.t: 我们的大脑使用这个系统来获取有关安全回家路线、高效觅食和规避危险的行为模式。

ex.s: We learn to tell the truth, even when lying is self-serving; we help a grandparent even when it is inconvenient.
ex.t: 我们学会说实话，即使撒谎对自己有利；我们在不方便的时候也会帮助祖父母。

ex.s: These abilities are strengthened by our capacity for language, which allows social practices to develop in extremely unobvious ways.
ex.t: 这些能力因我们的语言能力而增强，这使得社会实践能够以极其微妙的方式发展。

ex.s: Basic human needs lead to universal norms.
ex.t: 基本人类需求导致普遍规范。

ex.s: According to Isaiah Berlin, the hedgehog knows one thing very well, and the fox knows a lot of things.
ex.t: 根据以赛亚·伯林的说法，刺猬非常了解一件事，而狐狸了解很多事情。

ex.s: Hedgehog thinkers tend to answer yes. ___35___ And they are usually very credible in doing so.
ex.t: 刺猬型思考者倾向于回答是的。___35___而且他们在这样做时通常很有说服力。

ex.s: According to Jim Hart, the “hedgehog concept” is one of the factors that lead companies to greatness.
ex.t: 根据吉姆·哈特的看法，"刺猬理念"是导致公司卓越的因素之一。

ex.s: The advantage that foxes have is that they are more likely to seek out new information from a broader range of sources, and are comfortable with uncertainty and new information. ___38___ They try to include it in their viewpoint rather than to exclude it from their thinking.
ex.t: 狐狸的优势在于它们更有可能从更广泛的来源寻找新信息，并且对不确定性和新信息感到适应。___38___它们试图将其纳入自己的观点，而不是排除在思考之外。

ex.s: The most effective way to go through life is to try to be that rare mixture known as foxy hedgehog.
ex.t: 最有效的生活方式是努力成为那种被称为"狐狸式刺猬"的罕见混合体。

ex.s: They are more likely to remember people’s mistakes.
ex.t: 他们更容易记住人们的错误。

ex.s: But there can be a downside to concentration on one big thing.
ex.t: 但专注于一件事也可能有缺点。

ex.s: However, hedgehogs remain open to others’ reactions and inputs.
ex.t: 然而，刺猬仍然对其他人的反应和意见持开放态度。

ex.s: When something is contradictory to their view, they don’t treat it as exceptional.
ex.t: 当某事与他们的观点相矛盾时，他们不会将其视为例外。

ex.s: When I decided to pursue a postgraduate degree, I wanted to develop a novel research programme and quickly establish myself as an independent scientist.
ex.t: 当我决定攻读研究生学位时，我想开发一个新的研究计划，并迅速确立自己作为独立科学家的地位。

ex.s: But my need for independence drove me to push forward with my research plan.
ex.t: 但我对独立的需求驱使我继续推进我的研究计划。

ex.t: 到第四年，我对成功的渴望压倒了对独立的渴望。

ex.s: I worked extensively with other students, constantly asked questions, and helped with ongoing projects to learn everything I could.
ex.t: 我与其他学生广泛合作，不断提问，并参与正在进行的项目以学习一切我能学到的。

ex.s: By learning when to ask for help, I eventually found myself on the way to becoming an independent scientist.
ex.t: 通过学会何时寻求帮助，我终于踏上了成为独立科学家的道路。

ex.s: When John Todd was a child he loved to explore the woods around his house, observing how nature solved problems.
ex.t: 当约翰·托德还是个孩子的时候，他喜欢探索房子周围的树林，观察大自然如何解决问题。

ex.s: After studying agriculture, medicine, and fisheries in college, John went back to observing nature and asking questions.
ex.t: 在大学学习了农业、医学和渔业后，约翰回到观察大自然并提出问题。

ex.s: He decided to build what he would later call an eco-machine.
ex.t: 他决定建造他后来称之为"生态机器"的东西。

ex.t: 首先，他建造了一系列相互连接的透明玻璃纤维水箱。

ex.s: Then he went around to local ponds and streams and brought back some plants and animals.
ex.t: 然后他到当地的池塘和小溪转了一圈，带回一些植物和动物。

ex.s: The plants and animals in the eco-machine took the sludge as food and began to eat it!
ex.t: 生态机器中的植物和动物把污泥当作食物，开始吃掉它！

ex.t: "生态设计"是约翰对他所做工作的命名。

ex.t: 然后你让这些新系统发展出自我修复的方式。”

ex.s: The goal of this book is to make the case for digital minimalism, including a detailed exploration of what it asks and why it works, and then to teach you how to adopt this philosophy if you decide it’s right for you.
ex.t: 本书旨在阐明数字极简主义的主张，包括详细探讨它的要求以及它为何有效，然后教你在认为它适合你的情况下如何践行这一理念。

ex.s: To do so, I divided the book into two parts.
ex.t: 为此，我把这本书分成了两部分。

ex.s: In part one, I describe the philosophical foundations of digital minimalism, starting with an examination of the forces that are making so many people’s digital lives increasingly intolerable, before moving on to a detailed discussion of the digital minimalism philosophy.
ex.t: 在第一部分中，我阐述了数字极简主义的哲学基础，首先审视了使许多人的数字生活日益难以忍受的各种力量，然后详细讨论了数字极简主义哲学。

ex.s: This process requires you to step away from optional online activities for thirty days.
ex.t: 这个过程要求你在三十天内远离可有可无的线上活动。

ex.s: At the end of the thirty days, you will then add back a small number of carefully chosen online activities that you believe will provide massive benefits to the things you value.
ex.t: 三十天结束时，你再重新加入少量经过精心挑选的线上活动，即那些你认为能为你所珍视的事情带来巨大益处的活动。

ex.s: In doing so, I’ll draw on an experiment I ran in 2018 in which over 1,600 people agreed to perform a digital declutter.
ex.t: 在此过程中，我将引用我在2018年进行的一项实验，其中有1600多人同意进行数字清理。

ex.s: Each chapter concludes with a collection of practices, which are designed to help you act on the big ideas of the chapter.
ex.t: 每一章都以一组实践练习结尾，这些练习旨在帮助你把本章的重要观点付诸行动。

ex.s: Recommend them to friends.
ex.t: 把它们推荐给朋友。

ex.s: On March 7, 1907, the English statistician Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the “wisdom of crowds” effect.
ex.t: 1907年3月7日，英国统计学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿发表了一篇论文，阐述了后来被称为“群体智慧”效应的现象。

ex.s: Some people will tend to overestimate, and some to underestimate.
ex.t: 有些人倾向于高估，有些人倾向于低估。

ex.s: If people are similar and tend to make the same errors, then their errors won’t cancel each other out.
ex.t: 如果人们彼此相似并倾向于犯同样的错误，那么他们的错误就不会相互抵消。

ex.s: The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals.
ex.t: 该研究的关键发现是：当人群被进一步分成可以进行讨论的小组时，这些小组的平均值比同等数量的独立个体的平均值更准确。

ex.s: In a follow-up study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group members actually did in their discussion.
ex.t: 在一项有100名大学生参加的后续研究中，研究人员试图更好地了解小组成员在讨论中实际做了什么。

ex.s: Did they tend to go with those most confident about their estimates?
ex.t: 他们是否倾向于听从那些对自己的估算最自信的人？

ex.s: Did they follow those least willing to change their minds?
ex.t: 他们是否追随那些最不愿意改变主意的人？

ex.s: Fun to be around?
ex.t: 和你在一起很有趣吗？

ex.s: They don’t have to be world-changing, just aspects of your personality that you’re proud of.
ex.t: 它们不必是改变世界的壮举，只是你性格中让你感到自豪的方面。

ex.s: You could ask a friend or family member to help add to your list. ____19____ That way, you could exchange thoughts on what makes each of you special and the aspects of your personality that shine through.
ex.t: 你可以请朋友或家人帮你补充这个清单。____19____ 这样，你们就可以交流想法，谈谈是什么让彼此与众不同，以及你们性格中闪光的方面。

ex.s: In fact, don’t wait until you’ve made a mistake to try this — it’s a great way to boost self-confidence at any time.
ex.t: 事实上，不要等到犯了错误才尝试这样做——这在任何时候都是增强自信的好方法。

ex.t: 问题是，这是真的。____20____ 我们一直在改变和学习，而错误是发展和成长的积极方式。

ex.t: 在黄石体验野生动物（5月26日至9月2日）

ex.s: Learn where to look for animals and how to safely enjoy your wildlife watching experience.
ex.t: 学习在哪里寻找动物，以及如何安全地享受观察野生动物的体验。

ex.t: 少年护林员野生动物奥运会（6月5日至8月21日）

ex.s: Kids can test their skills and compare their abilities to the animals of Yellowstone.
ex.t: 孩子们可以测试自己的技能，并把自己的能力与黄石的动物们作比较。

ex.t: 探索为什么艺术家和摄影师一直被这个特别的地方所吸引。

ex.t: 该项目旨在帮助学生培养科学技能、环境意识和健康的生活方式。

ex.s: “The kids literally come to school with bags of snacks and large bottles of soft drinks,” she says.
ex.t: “孩子们真的是带着一袋袋零食和大瓶软饮料来上学的，”她说。

ex.s: “They come to us thinking vegetables are awful, dirt is awful, insects are awful.” Though some are initially scared of the insects and turned off by the dirt, most are eager to try something new.
ex.t: “他们来找我们时，认为蔬菜很讨厌，泥土很讨厌，昆虫很讨厌。”虽然有些人一开始害怕昆虫、厌恶泥土，但大多数人都渴望尝试新事物。

ex.s: “We have students who say they went home and talked to their parents and now they’re eating differently,” Jaramillo says.
ex.t: “我们有学生说，他们回家和父母谈过，现在他们的饮食方式不同了，”哈拉米略说。

ex.s: Besides, working in the garden seems to have a calming effect on Jaramillo’s special education students, many of whom have emotional control issues.
ex.t: 此外，在菜园里劳动似乎对哈拉米略的特殊教育学生有镇静作用，他们中许多人有情绪控制问题。

ex.s: We see scenes of children learning to read at home or at school, with the book as a focus for relations between the generations.
ex.t: 我们看到孩子们在家中或学校学习阅读的场景，书本成为几代人之间关系的焦点。

ex.s: These scenes may have been painted hundreds of years ago, but they record moments we can all relate to.
ex.t: 这些场景也许是数百年前画下的，但它们记录了我们每个人都能感同身受的时刻。

ex.s: Continued developments in communication technologies were once believed to make the printed page outdated.
ex.t: 通信技术的不断发展曾让人们以为印刷书页将会过时。

ex.s: To serve its function, a book must be activated by a user: the cover opened, the pages parted, the contents reviewed, perhaps notes written down or words underlined.
ex.t: 为了发挥其功能，一本书必须由使用者来激活：打开封面，翻开书页，浏览内容，也许还要写下笔记或划出字句。

ex.s: And in contrast to our increasingly networked lives where the information we consume is monitored and tracked, a printed book still offers the chance of a wholly private, “off-line” activity.
ex.t: 而且，与我们日益网络化的生活——我们所消费的信息受到监控和追踪——形成对比的是，印刷书仍然提供了一种完全私密的、“离线”活动的机会。

ex.s: As cities balloon with growth, access to nature for people living in urban areas is becoming harder to find.
ex.t: 随着城市不断膨胀扩张，生活在城市地区的人们越来越难接触到大自然。

ex.s: If you’re lucky, there might be a pocket park near where you live, but it’s unusual to find places in a city that are relatively wild.
ex.t: 如果运气好，你住的地方附近可能有一个口袋公园，但在城市里找到相对自然野性的地方是很少见的。

ex.s: They surveyed several hundred park-goers, asking them to submit a written summary online of a meaningful interaction they had with nature in the park.
ex.t: 他们调查了数百名游园者，请他们在线提交一份书面小结，描述他们在公园中与自然进行的一次有意义的互动。

ex.s: For example, one participant’s experience of “We sat and listened to the waves at the beach for a while” was assigned the categories “sitting at beach” and “listening to waves.”
ex.t: 例如，一位参与者的经历“我们在海滩上坐着听了一会儿海浪”被归入“坐在海滩上”和“听海浪”两个类别。

ex.s: Across the 320 submissions, a pattern of categories the researchers call a “nature language” began to emerge.
ex.t: 在320份提交材料中，一种被研究人员称为“自然语言”的类别模式开始显现。

ex.s: After the coding of all submissions, half a dozen categories were noted most often as important to visitors.
ex.t: 对所有提交材料进行编码后，有六种类别最常被游客提及为重要。

ex.s: Naming each nature experience creates a usable language, which helps people recognize and take part in the activities that are most satisfying and meaningful to them.
ex.t: 为每种自然体验命名创造出一种可用的语言，帮助人们认识并参与那些对他们来说最令人满足、最有意义的活动。

ex.s: “We’re trying to generate a language that helps bring the human-nature interactions back into our daily lives.
ex.t: “我们正试图创造一种语言，帮助把人与自然的互动带回我们的日常生活。

ex.s: Wild nature is hard to find in cities.
ex.t: 城市中很难找到自然野趣。

ex.s: People enjoy living close to nature.

ex.s: If you want to tell the history of the whole world, a history that does not privilege one part of humanity, you cannot do it through texts alone, because only some of the world has ever had texts, while most of the world, for most of the time, has not.
ex.t: 如果你想讲述整个世界的历史，一部不偏袒任何一部分人类的历史，你就不能只依靠文字文献，因为世界上只有一部分地区曾经有过文字，而世界上大部分地区在大部分时间里都没有。

ex.s: Ideally a history would bring together texts and objects, and some chapters of this book are able to do just that, but in many cases we simply can’t.
ex.t: 理想情况下，一部历史应该把文字和实物结合起来，本书的某些章节能够做到这一点，但在许多情况下我们根本做不到。

ex.s: If we want to reconstruct what was actually going on that day, the shield must be questioned and interpreted as deeply and strictly as the written reports.
ex.t: 如果我们想还原那天实际发生的事情，就必须像对待文字报告一样，深入而严格地追问和解读这面盾。

ex.s: In addition to the problem of miscomprehension from both sides, there are victories accidentally or deliberately twisted, especially when only the victors know how to write.
ex.t: 除了双方相互误解的问题之外，还有一些胜利被无意或有意地歪曲，尤其是当只有胜利者懂得书写的时候。

ex.s: Those who are on the losing side often have only their things to tell their stories.
ex.t: 处于失败一方的人往往只能用他们的物品来讲述自己的故事。

ex.s: The Caribbean Taino, the Australian Aboriginals, the African people of Benin and the Incas, all of whom appear in this book, can speak to us now of their past achievements most powerfully through the objects they made: a history told through things gives them back a voice.
ex.t: 加勒比海的泰诺人、澳大利亚原住民、贝宁的非洲人和印加人——他们都出现在本书中——如今可以通过他们制作的物品最有力地向我们讲述他们过去的成就：一部通过实物讲述的历史把声音还给了他们。

ex.s: If we are to find the other half of that conversation, we have to read not just the texts, but the objects.
ex.t: 如果我们要找到那场对话的另一半，我们就不仅要读文字，还要读实物。

ex.t: 我毫不犹豫地抓住了这个机会，几周后，当她邀请我与她讨论我可以在她的实验室里开展的潜在项目时，我同样震惊——而且欣喜若狂。

ex.s: What she proposed didn’t seem as exciting as the original project I had applied to, but I was going to give it my all.
ex.t: 她提出的方案看起来不如我最初申请的那个项目令人兴奋，但我决定全力以赴。

ex.s: In the end, I had a new scientific interest to pursue.
ex.t: 最终，我有了一个新的科学追求方向。

ex.s: When I applied to graduate school, I found three programmes promising to allow me to follow my desired research direction.
ex.t: 当我申请研究生院时，我发现有三个项目承诺允许我按照自己期望的研究方向发展。

ex.s: Rather than setting plans in stone, I’ve learned that sometimes I need to take the opportunities that are offered, even if they don’t sound perfect at the time, and make the most of them.
ex.t: 与其把计划定死，我学到了有时候我需要抓住提供的机会，即使当时听起来并不完美，并且充分利用它们。

ex.s: The inability to engage with longer-term causes and consequences leads to some of the world’s most serious problems: climate change, biodiversity collapse, and more.
ex.t: 无法关注长期的原因和后果导致了一些世界上最严重的问题：气候变化、生物多样性丧失等等。

ex.s: It is fair to say, though, that our psychological biases play a major role.
ex.t: 不过公平地说，我们的心理偏见起着主要作用。

ex.s: People’s hesitancy to delay satisfaction is the most obvious example, but there are others.
ex.t: 人们不愿意延迟满足是最明显的例子，但还有其他例子。

ex.s: Humans are unwilling to admit their shortcomings.
ex.t: 人类不愿承认自己的缺点。

ex.s: What does the author intend to tell us?
ex.t: 谦逊应是人类进步的动力。

ex.s: Humans tend to make long-term sacrifices.
ex.t: 人类倾向于做出长期的牺牲。

ex.s: The reason is simple: we know of just one type of life and it’s challenging to do science with a sample size of one.
ex.t: 原因很简单：我们只知道一种生命形式，而仅凭一个样本做科学是很有挑战性的。

ex.s: The field of artificial life-called ALife for short — is the systematic attempt to spell out life’s fundamental principles.
ex.t: 人工生命领域——简称ALife——是系统性地阐明生命基本原理的尝试。

ex.s: As much as many ALifers hate emphasizing their research’s applications, the attempts to create artificial life could have practical payoffs.
ex.t: 尽管许多ALife研究者不喜欢强调他们研究的实际应用，但创造人工生命的尝试可能会有实际的回报。

ex.s: This is the capacity for a system to create essentially endless complexity, to be a sort of “novelty generator”.
ex.t: 这是一个系统创造本质上无限复杂性的能力，成为一种"新颖性生成器"。

ex.s: The only system known to exhibit this is Earth’s biosphere.
ex.t: 已知唯一能展示这种能力的系统是地球的生物圈。

ex.s: If the field of ALife manages to reproduce life’s endless “creativity” in some virtual model, those same principles could give rise to truly inventive machines.
ex.t: 如果ALife领域能够在某些虚拟模型中复制生命无限的"创造力"，那么同样的原理可能会催生真正具有创造力的机器。

ex.s: Compared with the developments of Al, advances in ALife are harder to recognize.
ex.t: 与人工智能的发展相比，ALife的进展更难被识别。

ex.s: Undefined and uncontrolled, ALife drives its followers to repurpose old ideas and generated novelty.
ex.t: 未定义且不受控制的ALife推动其追随者重新利用旧思想并生成新事物。

ex.s: They may apply universally to all acts of evolution.
ex.t: 它们可能普遍适用于所有进化行为。

ex.s: ALife holds the key to human future.
ex.t: ALife掌握着人类未来的关键。

ex.s: Can Attempts to Create ALife Evolve, Too?
ex.t: 创造ALife的尝试也能进化吗？

ex.s: It’s a joyful and stressful time of year in the United States for students and their families as they make decisions about where to attend college.
ex.t: 对于美国的学生和家庭来说，这是一年中既快乐又充满压力的时期，因为他们要决定去哪所大学上学。

ex.s: Families often turn to rankings systems to help make a decision. ____35____
ex.t: 家庭经常借助排名系统来帮助做决定。____35____

ex.s: When I talk to families as a scholar of higher education, they’re often surprised that teaching excellence is not counted in rankings. ____36____
ex.t: 当我作为高等教育学者与家庭交谈时，他们常常惊讶地发现教学质量并未被计入排名。____36____

ex.s: Many instructors continue to teach using traditional lectures, which lead to lower success rates.
ex.t: 许多教师继续使用传统的讲授式教学，导致成功率较低。

ex.s: They should give strong consideration to universities where high-quality teaching is valued, even though the schools may be ranked lower.
ex.t: 他们应该认真考虑那些重视高质量教学的大学，即使这些学校的排名较低。

ex.s: Efforts to improve teaching at the university level have recently emerged.
ex.t: 大学层面改进教学的努力最近才出现。

ex.s: In fact, universities often shift emphasis from teaching to other ranking factors.
ex.t: 事实上，大学经常将重心从教学转移到其他排名因素上。

ex.s: For example, stress could serve as a cue that one responds to by eating, which produces the reward﹣the reduction of stress.
ex.t: 例如，压力可以作为提示，一个人通过进食来回应，从而产生奖励——压力的减轻。

ex.s: While a routine involves repeated behaviour, it’s not necessarily performed in response to a deep﹣rooted urge, as a habit is.
ex.t: 虽然常规涉及重复的行为，但不一定像习惯那样是对深层冲动的回应。

ex.s: Old habits can be difficult to shake, and healthy habits are often harder to develop.
ex.t: 旧习惯可能很难改掉，而健康习惯往往更难养成。

ex.s: But through repetition, it’s possible to form new habits.
ex.t: 但通过重复，有可能形成新的习惯。

ex.s: The amount of time needed to build a habit will depend on multiple factors, including the individual and the intended behaviour.
ex.t: 养成习惯所需的时间取决于多种因素，包括个人和预期行为。

ex.s: While you are able to pickup a new habit in a few weeks, it takes many months to build a healthy habit.
ex.t: 虽然你可以在几周内学会一个新习惯，但要养成健康习惯需要很多个月的时间。

ex.s: Take some time to think about what leads to bad habits and re﹣evaluate what you get out of them (or don’t).
ex.t: 花些时间思考导致坏习惯的原因，并重新评估你从中得到了什么（或者什么也没得到）。

ex.s: Consider and keep in mind why you want to make a change, including how the change reflects your values.
ex.t: 考虑并记住你为什么要做出改变，包括这种改变如何反映你的价值观。

ex.s: Some of my friends had signed up to spend time at a soup kitchen, so I did, too.

ex.t: 这看起来是件好事。

ex.s: I thought that we would just be passing out dinners to those in need, but I found out we would be doing everything from preparing to serving the dinner.
ex.t: 我以为我们只是分发晚餐给那些需要帮助的人，但我发现我们要做的事情从准备到服务晚餐无所不包。

ex.s: We began preparing the food, from mixing salad dressing to separating frozen meat.
ex.t: 我们开始准备食物，从调制沙拉酱到分拣冷冻肉类。

ex.s: I’d come face to face with the homeless: How should I act?
ex.t: 我将面对无家可归的人：我应该怎么做？

ex.s: I didn’t have too much time to worry about it.
ex.t: 我没有太多时间去担心这件事。

ex.s: Some looked like they had tally given up on life, while others seemed to be making the best of the situation, smiling and joking.
ex.t: 有些人看起来已经彻底放弃了生活，而另一些人似乎在尽力适应现状，微笑着开玩笑。

ex.s: Some were better off than others, but they all needed a good meal and a warm place to eat.
ex.t: 有些人的境况比别人好一点，但他们都需要一顿美餐和一个温暖的吃饭地方。

ex.s: It saddened me to think of how many people there were who didn’t have a place to call home and the only food they got came from a soup kitchen.
ex.t: 想到有那么多人没有家可回，唯一的食物来源就是施粥所，我感到难过。

ex.s: My perfectionist tendencies were the main root of this: I wanted to be perfect at whatever I did, which obviously in life is not possible, but it consumed me.
ex.t: 我的完美主义倾向是主要原因：我想在所做的任何事情上都做到完美，这在生活中显然是不可能的，但它吞噬了我。

ex.s: I joined a pre-presentation dinner with him and that smaller setting allowed me to slowly build up my courage to speak one-on-one with him—an idea that had seemed completely impossible.

ex.s: Each of these new steps continued to grow my confidence.

ex.s: According to systems thinking, changing the food system—or any other network—requires three things to happen.
ex.t: 根据系统思维，改变食物系统——或任何其他网络——需要三件事情发生。

ex.s: But using machine learning and artificial intelligence, some scientists propose that human diets consist of at least 26,000 biochemicals—and that the vast majority are not known.This shows that we have some way to travel before achieving the first objective of systems t hinking - which,in this example, is to identify more constituent parts of the nutrition system.
ex.t: 但利用机器学习和人工智能，一些科学家提出人类饮食至少包含26000种生化物质——其中绝大多数尚未被发现。这表明我们在实现系统思维的第一个目标方面还有很长的路要走——在本例中，这个目标是识别营养系统的更多组成部分。

ex.s: More researchers, policymakers and representatives from the food industry must learn to look beyond their direct lines of responsibility and adopt a systems approach.

ex.s: It is important to know from the beginning that there are a lot of highs and lows, and there is no such thing as overnight success.”

ex.t: 你看，他们中有很多人是去旅游的，要去迈阿密海滩和黄石公园这样的地方。

ex.t: 有一次，一位年轻女士在去南非探望家人的路上告诉我，她怀上了第一个孩子。

ex.s: To all, I wish a pleasant trip, to groups off for a family wedding in Singapore, to seniors travelling to Rome for holiday, to children off to Disney World in Orlando...the airport is not a dull place.
ex.t: 对所有人，我都祝愿旅途愉快——无论是去新加坡参加家庭婚礼的团队，还是去罗马度假的老人，或是去奥兰多迪士尼世界的孩子们……机场不是一个沉闷的地方。

ex.t: 有时我想，无论我们来自哪里，无论眼睛、头发和皮肤是什么颜色，我们来到这里都是为了表达理解并提供帮助。

ex.t: 使用吸力来抓取物体的动物通常生活在水中。

ex.t: 在科学领域，我们所做的既困难，而且往往也难以解释。

ex.s: The history of science offers many examples of matters that scientists thought they had resolved, only to discover that these matters needed to be reconsidered.
ex.t: 科学史提供了许多这样的例子：科学家们以为已经解决了的问题，后来却发现需要重新考虑。

ex.s: Recently a leading scientist said the scientific method was to avoid fooling oneself into thinking something is true that is not.
ex.t: 最近一位顶尖科学家说，科学方法是避免自欺欺人地相信不真实的事情。

ex.s: The good news is that when that happens, we pick ourselves up, brush ourselves off, and get back to work.
ex.t: 好消息是，当失败发生时，我们会重新站起来，拍掉身上的灰尘，继续工作。

ex.s: Understanding the world we live in, and using that knowledge to do useful things, is its own reward.
ex.t: 理解我们所生活的世界，并用这些知识做有用的事，本身就是一种回报。

ex.s: The most rewarding day for our group was project day，when all the efforts we put into collecting the items finally came together．When I saw the various supplies we had collected，it hit me that every kit we were to build that day would eventually be in the hands of an Iraqi child．Over the past four months，I had never imagined how I would feel once our project was completed．While making the kits，I realized that I had lost sight of the true meaning behind it．I had only focused on the fact that it was another school project and one I wanted to get a good grade on．When the kits were completed，and ready to be sent overseas，the warm feeling I had was one I would never forget．

ex.s: Recently，I conceptualized a new approach to timekeeping that's connected to circumstances on our planet，conditions that might change as a result of global warming．We're now building a clock at the Anchorage Museum that reflects the total flow of several major Alaskan rivers，which are sensitive to local and global environmental changes．We've programmed it to match an atomic clock if the waterways continue to flow at their present rate．If the rivers run faster in the future on average，the clock will get ahead of standard time．If they run slower，you'll see the opposite effect．
ex.t: 最近我构想了一种与地球环境状况相关联的新型计时方式这些状况可能因全球变暖而发生变化．我们正在安克雷奇博物馆建造一座钟它反映了几条主要阿拉斯加河流的总流量这些河流对当地和全球的环境变化都很敏感．我们已经编程让它在水流保持当前速率时与原子钟同步．如果将来河流平均流速加快钟会比标准时间走得快．如果河流变慢你会看到相反的效果．

ex.s: A．She wanted mom to read the news to her．
ex.t: 这是每个人学习阅读的方式。我们从句子开始，然后是段落，再然后是故事。这似乎是一场永无止境的旅程，但即使作为一个六岁的女孩，我就意识到知道如何阅读可以打开许多门。当妈妈说："糖果藏在顶层架子上，"我知道糖果在哪里。我在阅读方面的进步激发了我的好奇心，我想知道一切。我经常发现自己告诉妈妈开慢一点，这样我可以读出我们经过的所有路标。

ex.t: 然而，随着我逐渐成长，我曾经知道如此简单的世界正变得越来越复杂，我发现我需要一种逃避方式。通过打开一本小说，我可以把负担抛在脑后，进入一个美妙而神秘的世界，在那里我现在是一个新角色。在这些世界里我可以成为任何人。我不必写下发生了什么或者作者在写这本书时使用了什么技巧。我只是为了放松而读。

ex.s: The word history of typhoon had a far less direct path to the English language than gung-ho.
ex.t: 并非所有历史记载都是相同的。

ex.s: But, according to the Merriam-Webster New Book of Word Histories, the first typhoons reported in the English language were in India and were called “touffons” or “tufans,” The word tufan or al-tufan is Arabic and means violent storm or flood.
ex.t: 英国人在印度遇到这个单词并将其借入为touffon。

ex.s: The modern form of the word — typhoon — was influenced by the Cantonese but  ___40___ to make it appear more Greek.

ex.s: But for people families were destroyed by the super typhoon hit East China in July 2016, that summer was a time of great sadness.
ex.t: 但对于那些家庭被 2016 年 7 月袭击华东部、超级台风摧毁的人们来说，那个夏天是一段极度悲伤的时光。

ex.s: The floods and landslides caused by the typhoon killed 161 people, left 61 missing, and forced the evacuation of hundreds of thousands of people.
ex.t: 台风引发的洪水和山体滑坡造成 161 人死亡、61 人失踪，并迫使数十万人撤离。

ex.s: The victims the typhoon brought death or great loss were in several provinces along the Yangtze River.
ex.t: 遭受台风带来死亡或重大损失的人们，分布在长江沿岸的几个省份。

ex.s: Thunderstorms, floods, earthquakes, typhoons, volcanic eruptions, tsunamis, and forest fires have become increasingly common.
ex.t: 雷暴、洪水、地震、台风、火山喷发、海啸和森林火灾已变得越来越常见。
